### Describe the bug

When serving Kimi-K3 on a single 8-GPU B300 node, the scheduler occasionally stops making progress during chunked prefill. The HTTP process remains alive and continues serving `/v1/models` and `/metrics`, but the detokenizer heartbeat stops. Ten minutes later, the PyTorch NCCL watchdog aborts the scheduler processes.

This does not look like a generic NCCL transport timeout. In two independent occurrences, the same TP `ALLREDUCE` sequence number was submitted with different tensor sizes on different ranks. The tensors are outputs of `VocabParallelEmbedding` in the Kimi-K3 multimodal embedding path.

Occurrence 1:

```text
WorkNCCL SeqNum=1320347, OpType=ALLREDUCE

rank 0/1/2/3/4/6/7: NumelIn=4501504 = 628 * 7168
rank 5:             NumelIn=8171520 = 1140 * 7168
```

Occurrence 2:

```text
WorkNCCL SeqNum=1884583, OpType=ALLREDUCE

most ranks: NumelIn=43710464 = 6098 * 7168
rank 4:     NumelIn=69400576 = 9682 * 7168
```

`7168` is the Kimi-K3 hidden size, so these sizes correspond to different token-row counts entering the same TP collective. NCCL waits because the collective contract has already diverged across ranks.

## Impact

- All in-flight generation requests stop making progress.
- Health checks begin failing because no detokenizer heartbeat is received.
- The NCCL watchdog waits for the configured 600-second distributed timeout.
- PyTorch then raises `c10::DistBackendError` and aborts the scheduler with exit code `-6` (`SIGABRT`).
- The service requires a process/container restart to recover.

We do not yet have a single-request deterministic reproducer. The failure has occurred twice under production traffic with the following common conditions:

Host available memory decreases from approximately 295 GiB before loading to
approximately 89 GiB while the transformer is being loaded. The 2 GiB swap is
also exhausted.

The process then dies while loading the approximately 38 GiB DiT:

```text
Loading QwenImageTransformer2DModel from 9 safetensors file(s)
...
Rank 0 scheduler is dead
Exit code: -9
EOFError
```

The other NCCL/TCPStore errors occur after rank 0 has already disappeared and
appear to be secondary failures.

### Control experiments

#### 1. Diffusers backend

The Diffusers backend can start successfully:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
sglang serve \
  --backend diffusers \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image \
  --num-gpus 4 \
  --sp-degree 4 \
  --text-encoder-cpu-offload \
  --vae-cpu-offload
```

This control uses a different execution/loading path and is included only to
show that the checkpoint itself is valid and can be loaded on this machine.

#### 2. Native single-GPU pipeline

The native pipeline works on one GPU when the DiT is GPU-resident:

```bash
HF_ENDPOINT=https://huggingface.co \
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
sglang serve \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image \
  --num-gpus 1 \
  --sp-degree 1 \
  --dit-cpu-offload false \
  --text-encoder-cpu-offload \
  --vae-cpu-offload \
  --pin-cpu-memory false
```

At 512×512, the observed peak reserved GPU memory is approximately 42.1 GiB.

#### 3. Native SP=4 without DiT CPU offload

The native SP=4 pipeline is still killed by the host OOM killer during
transformer loading with:

```text
--dit-cpu-offload false --pin-cpu-memory false
```

This suggests that the failure is related to the transient multi-rank loading
peak, rather than only the final CPU-resident model size or pinned memory.

### Expected behavior

The native SP=4 pipeline should do at least one of the following:

- avoid materializing full temporary checkpoint states independently on every
  rank;
- load or shard weights directly to their destination devices;
- stagger rank loading to limit peak host memory;
- support effective FSDP weight sharding for Qwen-Image;
- document the required host-memory capacity;
- or fail early with a clear host-memory diagnostic instead of being silently
  killed by the OS.

### Suspected cause

This is a hypothesis based on code inspection and has not yet been confirmed.

Sequence parallelism splits the latent sequence but does not shard the DiT
weights. With `use_fsdp_inference=false`, every SP rank loads the complete
Qwen-Image transformer.

In addition, `hf_to_custom_state_dict()` consumes the checkpoint iterator into
a complete `custom_param_sd` before
`load_model_from_full_model_state_dict()` constructs the state passed to
`model.load_state_dict()`.

During dtype/device/offload conversion, checkpoint tensors, converted tensors,
and final parameters may coexist temporarily. When four ranks perform this
work concurrently, the transient host-memory requirement may scale with the
number of ranks.

Relevant code:

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/utils.py`
- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/fsdp_load.py`

A potentially related report for another diffusion model is:

- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34902

### Reproduction

Model: `Qwen/Qwen-Image`

```bash
HF_ENDPOINT=https://huggingface.co \
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
/opt/conda/envs/sgl-diffusion/bin/sglang serve \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30010 \
  --num-gpus 4 \
  --sp-degree 4 \
  --text-encoder-cpu-offload \
  --vae-cpu-offload \
  --pin-cpu-memory
```

The native pipeline is selected successfully:

```text
Using pipeline from model_index.json: QwenImagePipeline
```

Host memory usage then grows rapidly while loading:

```text
Loading QwenImageTransformer2DModel from 9 safetensors file(s)
```

Eventually rank 0 is killed by the host OOM killer:

```text
Rank 0 scheduler is dead
Exit code: -9
EOFError
```

The subsequent NCCL/TCPStore errors occur after rank 0 has been killed.

title: [Bug] Reasoning parsers: text before the opening think token is routed four different ways (chunk-dependent, and one-shot keeps the literal marker)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`BaseReasoningFormatDetector` decides that a text is a reasoning block with
`self.think_start_token in text` (the marker anywhere), but removes the marker
with `while processed_text.startswith(think_start_text)` (the marker at index 0).
Anything the model writes in front of the opening marker — including a single
space or newline — falls into that gap.

The streaming path has the mirror-image gap: it only recognises a partial opening
marker when the *whole* buffer is a prefix of it, so a chunk that carries content
first (`"Sure."` + `"<"`) clears the buffer and the rest of the marker arrives
with nothing to attach to.

Same string, four different answers on `main` (`b6d760291`, `--reasoning-parser qwen3`):

| path | `reasoning_content` | `content` |
|---|---|---|
| non-streaming `detect_and_parse` | `'Sure.<think>checking'` | `'Done.'` |
| streaming, marker whole in one chunk | `'checking'` | `'Sure.Done.'` |
| streaming, chunk ends inside `<think>` | `''` | `'Sure.<think>checking</think>Done.'` |
| streaming, whole turn in one chunk | `'Sure.checking'` | `'Done.'` |

Row 1 hands the client a literal `<think>` inside `reasoning_content`. Row 3 is
the damaging one: the entire reasoning block, markers included, is streamed as
assistant content and `reasoning_content` is empty.

### Reproduction

CPU only, no model needed:

```python
from sglang.srt.parser.reasoning_parser import ReasoningParser

TEXT = "Sure.<think>checking</think>Done."

def stream(chunks):
    p = ReasoningParser(model_type="qwen3")
    r = n = ""
    for c in chunks:
        a, b = p.parse_stream_chunk(c)
        r += a or ""; n += b or ""
    a, b = p.parse_stream_end()
    return r + (a or ""), n + (b or "")

print(ReasoningParser(model_type="qwen3").parse_non_stream(TEXT))
print(stream(["Sure.", "<think>", "checking", "</think>", "Done."]))
print(stream(["Sure.<", "think>", "checking", "</think>", "Done."]))
print(stream([TEXT]))
```

```
('Sure.<think>checking', 'Done.')
('checking', 'Sure.Done.')
('', 'Sure.<think>checking</think>Done.')
('Sure.checking', 'Done.')
```

A single leading newline is enough for the non-streaming half — this is the
common shape, not a contrived one:

```python
ReasoningParser(model_type="qwen3").parse_non_stream("\n<think>checking</think>Done.")
# ('\n<think>checking', 'Done.')   <- the marker reaches the client
```

### Mechanism

`python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py`

- One-shot, `_detect_and_parse_impl`: `in_reasoning` is decided by
  `think_start_token in text` (any position), but the strip loop is
  `startswith`. With a lead the marker is never removed, and the lead itself is
  classified as reasoning.
- Streaming, `_parse_streaming_increment_impl`:
  - the strip is `current_text.replace(think_start_text, "", 1)` with no split of
    what preceded it, so a lead that arrives in the same buffer as the marker is
    absorbed into reasoning;
  - the not-in-reasoning branch ends with `self._buffer = ""` and emits the whole
    buffer as content — no `_ends_with_partial_token` holdback for the *opening*
    marker, unlike the in-reasoning branch which holds back the closing one.
    That is row 3.

### When row 3 is reachable

It needs one chunk to carry content followed by a strict prefix of the opening
marker. With `stream_interval=1` and `<think>` as a single special token that
cannot happen; it becomes reachable when a decode step delivers several tokens at
once — `--stream-interval > 1`, `sampling_params.stream_interval`, speculative
decoding, or the detokenizer releasing several tokens after holding an incomplete
UTF-8 sequence. Rows 1, 2 and 4 need no such condition.

### Blast radius

19 of the 26 entries in `ReasoningParser.DetectorMap` — every one that inherits
the base implementations: `deepseek-r1`, `deepseek-v3`, `deepseek-v4`, `glm45`,
`hunyuan`, `kimi`, `kimi_k2`, `mimo`, `poolside_v1`, `qwen3`, `qwen3-thinking`,
`minimax`, `minimax-m3`, `step3`, `step3p5`, `mistral`, `nemotron_3`, `interns1`,
`gemma4`. (`gpt-oss`, `kimi_k3`, `muse`, `inkling`, `apertus2509`,
`cohere_command4` override both methods and are not affected by this specific
gap.)

### Related

`TestStreamingChunkSizeInvariance` in
`test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py`, added by #34458, already
names this case and pins it as a known exception:

```python
def test_text_before_think_token_is_chunk_dependent(self):
    """Accepted divergence, inherited from main: text before `<think>` lands
    in reasoning or content depending on where the chunk boundary falls."""
```

That test asserts the three streaming variants and the fourth one-shot split as
the expected outcome. This issue is a request to close that exception rather than
keep it pinned.

### Expected behaviour

The block opens at the marker, so the routing should not depend on chunking:

- the marker is removed wherever it first appears, not only at index 0;
- text in front of it is content — except under `force_reasoning`, where the
  chat template already opened the block, and it is reasoning;
- both are what the streaming path already does when the marker happens to land
  whole at a chunk start.

I have a fix and regression tests ready (the four rows collapse to one, and the
pinned test above becomes an invariance test). Happy to open the PR.

### Environment

`main` @ `b6d760291`, CPU-only unit environment, Python 3.12.

title: Tool-call parsers lose or corrupt data at streaming chunk boundaries (multiple detectors)
body:
A sweep of `function_call/` found several streaming/parse bugs, all reproduced by feeding text to the real detector classes. Common root causes: (a) streaming state machines with no end-of-stream `_buffer` flush (`function_call_parser.parse_stream_chunk` never flushes, and `serving_chat._check_for_unstreamed_tool_args` only rescues the last tool's trailing args and bails when `prev_tool_call_arr` is empty); (b) hand-rolled brace/bracket/token counting that ignores string-literal context; (c) regex written for the happy path applied to the whole buffer / untrusted output.

**Data loss (drops arguments or whole tool calls):**
- `base_format_detector.parse_streaming_increment` (name-send branch, ~`:244-271`) emits the tool name and returns without emitting args, without populating `prev_tool_call_arr`, and without advancing `_buffer`. With coarse chunking (batched detok, `stream_interval>1`, speculative decode) 2 parallel tool calls lose data in **71% (Qwen25) / 91% (Hermes)** of random 1-4 chunk splits; a single tool call in one chunk streams `arguments: ""`. Affects Qwen25/Hermes/Mistral/Llama32/GLM4/DeepSeekV3.
- `step3_detector.py:264,318`: `param_regex.finditer(invoke_part)` is not bounded by `</steptml:invoke>`, so with two calls the second is dropped and its params are grafted onto the first.
- `kimik2_detector.py:394`: `_split_pending_start` range stops at 2, so a lone trailing `<` (prefix of both section/call begin tokens) is not held back -> the whole call is dropped and raw tokens leak to normal_text.

**Corruption (emits invalid JSON / mangled text):**
- `kimik2_detector.py:316-320`: when `<|tool_call_end|>` splits across a chunk, `args_full = buffer[args_start:]` includes the partial end-token prefix and streams it as argument content (never retracted) -> `json.loads` raises `Extra data`.
- `deepseekv3_detector.py:114-118`: the greedy DOTALL streaming regex `...<sep>(.*)\n\`\`\`json...` spans two calls in one increment, so `tool_index 0` gets the second tool's name.
- `llama32_detector.py:124-125`: `re.sub(r"'([^']*)':", ...)` over the whole buffer injects a `\"` inside JSON string values that contain `'x':` or `: 'x'`, truncating them (e.g. an arg echoing a dict literal).
- `deepseekv3_detector.py:72-86` (+ v31): the per-call loop is in one `try`; a single malformed call jumps to `except`, discarding already-parsed valid calls and returning the raw markup as normal_text.

**Prose corruption / off-by-one:**
- `base_format_detector.py:160-161` / `mistral_detector.py:133-134`: `normal_text.replace(self.eot_token, "")` with Mistral `eot_token="]"` deletes every `]` in ordinary assistant text (`"item[0] done"` -> `"item[0 done"`).
- `llama32_detector.py:72`: `idx += end + len(tool_call_separator)` assumes a `;` always follows a decoded object, so trailing normal text with no separator loses its first char.
- `pythonic_detector._find_matching_bracket:113-133` counts `[`/`]` without respecting string literals, so a string arg containing `]` mis-slices the call and it is dropped in streaming.

Each is individually reproducible against the real detector. Same family as the recently-fixed streaming-detok duplication -- streaming state that loses/corrupts data at chunk boundaries. Happy to send PRs for the self-contained ones (e.g. the Mistral `]` strip, the Llama32 first-char drop, the DeepSeek discard-all-on-error) if the direction is welcome.

cc @JustinTong0323 @CatherineSue

title: [Bug] DeepSeek V3.2/V4 DSML detector strips whitespace (e.g. trailing newline) from string="true" parameter values
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`DeepSeekV32Detector` and `DeepSeekV4Detector` (`--tool-call-parser deepseekv32` / `deepseekv4`) call `.strip()` on raw `string="true"` parameter values (`strip_string_param_value = True` in `deepseekv32_detector.py`). Leading and trailing whitespace that belongs to the value is lost. The most common case is a file's trailing newline in a `write_file`-style call, so file contents written by an agent are silently altered. Streaming gives the same stripped value.

DeepSeek's reference implementations keep the value byte-for-byte. The encoder writes the value verbatim, and `parse_message_from_completion_text` in both `encoding_dsv32.py` and `encoding_dsv4.py` reads it with `(.*?)<$`, which does not strip. On main, `DeepSeekV41Detector` already sets `strip_string_param_value = False`. PR #39665 kept V3.2/V4 unchanged, so those two still differ from the reference.

**Expected:** `content` is `'def f():\n    return 1\n'`, which is what DeepSeek's `parse_message_from_completion_text` returns for the same text.

### Reproduction

CPU only, with no model or server:

```python
import json
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.deepseekv32_detector import DeepSeekV32Detector
from sglang.srt.function_call.deepseekv4_detector import DeepSeekV4Detector

tools = [Tool(type="function", function=Function(name="write_file", parameters={
    "type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}, "content": {"type": "string"}}}))]
content = "def f():\n    return 1\n"  # file ends with a newline
for det, block in ((DeepSeekV32Detector, "function_calls"), (DeepSeekV4Detector, "tool_calls")):
    text = (f"<｜DSML｜{block}>\n<｜DSML｜invoke name=\"write_file\">\n"
            "<｜DSML｜parameter name=\"path\" string=\"true\">f.py</｜DSML｜parameter>\n"
            f"<｜DSML｜parameter name=\"content\" string=\"true\">{content}</｜DSML｜parameter>\n"
            f"</｜DSML｜invoke>\n</｜DSML｜{block}>")
    got = json.loads(det().detect_and_parse(text, tools).calls[0].parameters)["content"]
    print(det.__name__, "expected", repr(content), "got", repr(got))
```

The output is the same on the v0.5.20 wheel and on main `3ed56a3`:

```
DeepSeekV32Detector expected 'def f():\n    return 1\n' got 'def f():\n    return 1'
DeepSeekV4Detector expected 'def f():\n    return 1\n' got 'def f():\n    return 1'
```

For comparison, DeepSeek-V3.2's own `encoding/encoding_dsv32.py` (`parse_message_from_completion_text(text + "<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>", thinking_mode="chat")`) returns `"content": "def f():\n    return 1\n"`, and the V4 `encoding_dsv4.py` does the same.

Fixtures (official-encoder renders, replayed as token ids through the serving-layer code; the expected values come from DeepSeek's reference parser):
- [`deepseek/v32-unescaped-string-value`](https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall/blob/35b19e33ea38c406bf8aa910550841e601aadb59/fixtures/deepseek/v32.jsonl#L14)
- [`deepseek/v4-unescaped-string-value`](https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall/blob/35b19e33ea38c406bf8aa910550841e601aadb59/fixtures/deepseek/v4.jsonl#L15)

### Environment

This is parser-level only (CPU, macOS arm64, no GPU). It was verified on the `sglang==0.5.20` wheel and on main `3ed56a341b57eb57c8e37e0cec353e67ebb35c3b`. `python3 -m sglang.check_env`, trimmed:

```
Python: 3.12.13 (main, Jun 11 2026, 03:55:21) [Clang 22.1.3 ]
MPS available: True
macOS Version: 26.5.1
Apple Silicon: Apple M4 Max
PyTorch: 2.13.0
sglang: 0.5.20
transformers: 5.12.1
pydantic: 2.13.5
xgrammar: 0.2.1
```

Found by canitoolcall (https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall), an offline conformance suite for tool-call parsers. This report was drafted with AI assistance, and the repro above was run and its output pasted verbatim.

title: [Bug] Gemma4Detector returns null and exponent-notation numbers as strings
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`Gemma4Detector` (`--tool-call-parser gemma4`) turns two kinds of bare values into JSON strings:

- `null` becomes `"null"`.
- Numbers in exponent notation, such as `1e-05` or `1e+21`, become `"1e-05"` and `"1e+21"`.

The Gemma 4 chat template renders `None` as `null`, and it renders small or large floats in exponent form. So a call round-tripped through the official template does not parse back to its original arguments, and the result fails a schema that declares `number` / `null`.

The cause is in `_parse_gemma4_value` in `python/sglang/srt/function_call/gemma4_detector.py`:
- It handles `true` and `false` but not `null`.
- It picks `float()` only when the text contains `"."`. `int("1e-05")` then raises, and the value falls through to "bare string".

The behavior is the same in non-streaming and streaming.

**Expected:** `{"exact": true, "limit": null, "tolerance": 1e-05, "values": [0, -0.5, 1e+21], "x": -3, "y": 2.5}`

### Reproduction

CPU only, with no model or server:

```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.gemma4_detector import Gemma4Detector

tools = [Tool(type="function", function=Function(name="calculate", parameters={
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
        "x": {"type": "integer"}, "y": {"type": "number"},
        "tolerance": {"type": "number"}, "exact": {"type": "boolean"},
        "limit": {"type": ["integer", "null"]},
        "values": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "number"}},
    }}))]
# Gemma 4 chat template rendering of calculate(x=-3, y=2.5, tolerance=1e-05, exact=True, limit=None, values=[0, -0.5, 1e+21])
text = "<|tool_call>call:calculate{exact:true,limit:null,tolerance:1e-05,values:[0,-0.5,1e+21],x:-3,y:2.5}<tool_call|>"
print(Gemma4Detector().detect_and_parse(text, tools).calls[0].parameters)
```

title: [Bug] gpt-oss detector misses tool calls that are the first message or lack <|constrain|>json
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`GptOssDetector` (`--tool-call-parser gpt-oss`) only recognises a tool call written exactly as `<|start|>assistant<|channel|>commentary to=functions.X ... <|constrain|>json<|message|>...`. Two other valid Harmony shapes are missed in non-streaming:

- **B. The call is the first message of the completion.** The generation prompt already ends with `<|start|>assistant`, so a call the model emits without an analysis message first starts with `<|channel|>commentary to=...`. `has_tool_call()` checks for `bot_token = "<|start|>assistant<|channel|>commentary"`, finds nothing, and the raw Harmony markup is returned as `content`. The streaming path parses the same text correctly, so the two paths disagree.
- **C. The call has no `<|constrain|>json`.** The Harmony format treats `<|constrain|>` as optional. `tool_extract_pattern` requires `<|constrain|>json<|message|>`, so the call is dropped and `content` is empty. The request returns neither a tool call nor text. Streaming drops it too.

There is also a lower-priority case:

- **D. The recipient is in the role header** (`<|start|>assistant to=functions.X<|channel|>commentary ...`). The Harmony spec allows it ("The recipient might be defined in the role or channel section of the header", `docs/format.md`), and openai-harmony renders history that way. Here the whole call comes back as content. Generations usually put the recipient after the channel, so this one matters mostly for replayed or third-party outputs.

**Expected:** a `get_weather` tool call with `{"city": "Paris"}` in B, C and D, as in A.

Code: `python/sglang/srt/function_call/gpt_oss_detector.py` (`bot_token`, `has_tool_call`, `tool_extract_pattern`). This file is unchanged between v0.5.20 and main `3ed56a3`.

### Reproduction

CPU only, with no model or server. The script uses the parser classes in the same order `serving_chat` does (reasoning parser, then tool-call parser):

```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.gpt_oss_detector import GptOssDetector
from sglang.srt.parser.reasoning_parser import ReasoningParser

tools = [Tool(type="function", function=Function(name="get_weather", parameters={
    "type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}}))]
ANALYSIS = "<|channel|>analysis<|message|>Need the weather.<|end|><|start|>assistant"
CALL = '<|channel|>commentary to=functions.get_weather <|constrain|>json<|message|>{"city": "Paris"}<|call|>'
NO_CONSTRAIN = '<|channel|>commentary to=functions.get_weather<|message|>{"city": "Paris"}<|call|>'
ROLE_RECIPIENT = ('<|start|>assistant to=functions.get_weather<|channel|>commentary <|constrain|>json'
                  '<|message|>{"city": "Paris"}<|call|>')
cases = {
    "A. analysis, then call (works)": ANALYSIS + CALL,
    "B. call is the first message": CALL,
    "C. analysis, then call without <|constrain|>json": ANALYSIS + NO_CONSTRAIN,
    "D. recipient in the role header": "<|channel|>analysis<|message|>Need the weather.<|end|>" + ROLE_RECIPIENT,
}
for label, text in cases.items():
    # same order as serving_chat: reasoning parser first, then the tool-call parser
    _, rest = ReasoningParser(model_type="gpt-oss").parse_non_stream(text)
    res = GptOssDetector().detect_and_parse(rest, tools)
    print(label)
    print("   calls:", [(c.name, c.parameters) for c in res.calls], "| content:", repr(res.normal_text))
```

The output is identical on the v0.5.20 wheel and on main `3ed56a3` (`PYTHONPATH=<checkout>/python`):

```
A. analysis, then call (works)
   calls: [('get_weather', '{"city": "Paris"}')] | content: ''
B. call is the first message
   calls: [] | content: '<|channel|>commentary to=functions.get_weather <|constrain|>json<|message|>{"city": "Paris"}<|call|>'
C. analysis, then call without <|constrain|>json
   calls: [] | content: ''
D. recipient in the role header
   calls: [] | content: '<|start|>assistant to=functions.get_weather<|channel|>commentary <|constrain|>json<|message|>{"city": "Paris"}<|call|>'
```

For B, `GptOssDetector().parse_streaming_increment(CALL, tools)` returns the `get_weather` call, so only non-streaming misses it.

These fixtures replay the same shapes, with the gpt-oss-20b tokenizer's token ids, through the serving-layer code:
- B: [`gpt-oss/harmony-test-channel-first-constrain-adjacent`](https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall/blob/35b19e33ea38c406bf8aa910550841e601aadb59/fixtures/gpt-oss/imported.jsonl#L18) (from openai/harmony's `tests/test_harmony.py`)

- D: [`gpt-oss/harmony-single-call`](https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall/blob/35b19e33ea38c406bf8aa910550841e601aadb59/fixtures/gpt-oss/rendered.jsonl#L1), an openai-harmony render

### Environment

title: [Bug] Qwen3 Coder buffers large string tool-call arguments during streaming
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

The Qwen3 Coder tool-call parser currently buffers string parameter values until it sees `</parameter>` or another terminating tag.

For large string arguments, such as a `write_file` tool with a long `content` field, this means OpenAI-compatible streaming clients do not receive incremental `delta.tool_calls[].function.arguments` fragments while the content is being generated. Instead, the whole string argument is emitted as one large chunk only after the closing parameter tag arrives.

This breaks the expected streaming behavior for tool calls with large string fields. Clients that render or process tool-call arguments incrementally cannot observe progress until the full parameter is complete.

### Expected behavior

For string-like parameters, Qwen3 Coder streaming should emit argument fragments progressively as the value arrives, while preserving valid JSON across chunks. For example, after receiving the beginning of a large `content` parameter, the stream should already include something like:

```text
{"content": "<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html>\n...
```

before the parser has seen the final `</parameter>` token.

Non-string parameters such as booleans, integers, arrays, and objects can continue using the existing complete-value parsing path.

### Actual behavior

The parser emits the parameter key and value only after the closing parameter tag is seen. With a long `content` value, the client gets one large `delta.tool_calls[].function.arguments` chunk at the end instead of incremental chunks during generation.

### Reproduction

A minimal parser-level reproduction is a Qwen3 Coder tool call where a string parameter is split across streaming chunks and the closing `</parameter>` tag is delayed or split:

```text
<tool_call>
<function=write_file>
<parameter=file_path>/tmp/demo.html</parameter>
<parameter=content>
<!DOCTYPE html>\n
<html>\n
<body>hello</body>\n
</par
ameter>
<parameter=overwrite>false</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

When these chunks are fed through `Qwen3CoderDetector.parse_streaming_increment`, no incremental `content` argument fragments are emitted before the content parameter closes. The `content` argument is buffered until `</parameter>` is complete.

### Suggested fix

Stream schema string-like parameters incrementally in `Qwen3CoderDetector`, while keeping the existing complete-value path for non-string parameters.

A proposed implementation and regression test are already available in PR #25246:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25246

That PR verifies that a long `content` parameter emits before `</parameter>` is received, and that the final accumulated JSON remains valid.

### Environment

This is a parser-only issue in the Qwen3 Coder function-call detector. It does not depend on CUDA kernels, model forward execution, scheduling, or token generation speed.

Observed against the current `main` branch behavior before PR #25246.

title: [Feature][DSv4.1] Tracking: every backend's two-level candidate indexer behind CandidateIndexer
body:
## Context

DeepSeek-V4.1's low-ratio index layers select attention positions in two levels: the candidate source (layer 20) keeps the best `candidate_topk_blocks = 2048` blocks of 8 compressed positions per query row, the consumers (24 / 28 / 32 / 36) run their top-512 among those blocks. PR [#40352](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40352) put the prefill side of that behind one interface, `CandidateIndexer` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/candidate_indexer.py`):

```python
class CandidateIndexer(ABC):
    def publish_prefill(self, inputs: PrefillIndexerInputs, out_positions) -> CandidateMetadata
    def select_prefill(self, published, inputs, out_positions) -> None
    def prefill_tail(self, published, tail_lens) -> CandidateMetadata
```

with two implementations, and the decode side already had one:

| implementation | file | prefill | decode / verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DeepGemmCandidateIndexer` (SM100) | `dsv4/candidate_indexer_deep_gemm.py` | block table from the source's dense tiles (`amax8_varlen`, ragged top-k, `sort_candidate_blocks`, DeepGEMM schedule); consumers score only their blocks with `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` + `topk_transform_bf16_small` | `publish_decode` / `select_decode`, same kernels over the paged index-K pool |
| `DenseCandidateIndexer` | `dsv4/dense_prefill_indexer.py` | #40217's `dense_prefill_topk`: block ids per request (`PrefillCandidateBlocks`), consumers rebuild a mask per 2 GiB tile and run the plain top-k | — |

`make_candidate_indexer` returns the DeepGEMM indexer on SM100 (with the dense one for prefill under context parallelism) and `None` on everything else. The backend's dense prefill path (`_low_ratio_index_topk_dense`) only calls the three methods; on 4x B200 at 262K context that took the four consumer layers from 41 ms to 2.6 ms each and TTFT from 6.7 s to 5.3 s.

Everything else still scores the whole context and selects through masks inline in `deepseek_v4_backend.py`, or has no DSv4.1 low-ratio path at all. This issue lists what is left, per backend and mode, with the code that has to move.

## Where the candidate indexer runs today

| platform / mode | entry point | how candidates are handled | cost per index layer |
|---|---|---|---|
| SM100 CUDA (and `DeepseekV4TrtllmAttnBackend`, which inherits it), decode + target-verify | `_low_ratio_index_topk_decode` -> `DeepGemmCandidateIndexer.publish_decode` / `select_decode` | block table + DeepGEMM sparse logits; graph variants `candidate_all` / `candidate_c2_all` / `candidate_unfiltered` / `candidate_filtered` (`graph_variants.py`, `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`) | consumers score 2048 x 8 positions |
| SM100 CUDA, extend (dense fp4 path) | `_low_ratio_index_topk_dense` -> `CandidateIndexer` | block table, consumers sparse | source 43.5 ms, consumer 2.6 ms at 16K rows x 262K |
| SM100 CUDA, extend under CP (`_forward_low_ratio_sources_cp`) | same, but `make_candidate_indexer` hands the DeepGEMM indexer a `DenseCandidateIndexer` for prefill | dense tiles + masks | consumer 41 ms |
| SM100 CUDA, extend inside the prefill CUDA graph | `_low_ratio_index_topk_prefill_graph` | none needed: asserts `width <= candidate_topk_blocks * candidate_block_size`, so every block is a candidate and the plain top-k is the whole selection | — |
| SM90 CUDA, decode + verify | `_low_ratio_index_topk_sm90_decode` | **inline**: Triton `fp4_index_logits_decode` scores all `[B, L]` positions per index layer; the source builds `CandidateMasks(mask=[B, L] bool)` with `select_candidate_blocks`; consumers `masked_fill` + `torch.topk` + `mask_topk_scores` | full context per consumer |
| SM90 CUDA, extend (and SM100 with `SGLANG_DSV41_TORCH_PREFILL_INDEXER=1`) | `_low_ratio_index_topk_torch` | **inline**: per request, per row chunk, bf16 einsum over dequantized K (`get_low_ratio_index_k_dequant`); source publishes `CandidateMasks(request_masks=[[rows_b, lc_b] bool])`, consumers mask + `torch.topk`; the tail cut goes through `_publish_prefill_masks` / `cut_request_masks` | full context per consumer, plus the masks |
| ROCm (`DeepseekV4HipRadixBackend`, selected for `dsv4` on HIP in `attention_registry.py`) | — | no ratio-1/2 (`low_ratio`) path at all: the backend carries the V4 C4 indexer only (`C4IndexerBackendMixin`); its metadata only knows compress ratios 0 / 4 / 128 | DSv4.1 not served |
| NPU (`DeepseekV4AscendAttnBackend`) | — | no DSv4.1 low-ratio path | DSv4.1 not served |

`make_candidate_indexer` and the graph variants are gated on `device_sm >= 100` / `not is_hip()`, so on every non-SM100 target the protocol is simply absent.

## Work items

### 1. Hopper decode / verify behind the protocol, consumers scoring candidates only

`_low_ratio_index_topk_sm90_decode` (backend ~L3475) is the only decode path outside `CandidateIndexer`. Today each consumer layer scores `[bs, L]` for the whole context and masks 15 of every 16 columns away, and the graph variants of `graph_variants.py` are not built for it.

- Add `publish_decode` / `select_decode` to the `CandidateIndexer` ABC (they exist on `DeepGemmCandidateIndexer` only) and move the SM90 code into an implementation, so the backend's decode dispatch is `self.candidate_indexer.publish_decode(...)` / `select_decode(...)` on every platform.
- Consumer scoring: there is no DeepGEMM paged sparse kernel below SM100. Options: extend `fp4_index_logits_decode` (Triton, `kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/fp4_indexer.py`) with a block-id input so it reads only the 2048 blocks per row (`slots[b, blocks[b, i // 8] * 8 + i % 8]`), or reuse the gathering Triton scorer of #40268 (`candidate_fp4_mqa_logits`, contiguous K) once it takes per-row block ids for a batch.
- Decode graph variants for SM90 once the selection has a fixed shape.

### 2. Torch prefill path behind the protocol

`_low_ratio_index_topk_torch` (backend ~L3555) is Hopper's prefill indexer and the SM100 test oracle. Its publish / consume is interleaved with the per-request row-chunk loop, so it does not fit `publish_prefill` / `select_prefill` as written.

- Restructure into a `TorchCandidateIndexer` (or fold into `DenseCandidateIndexer` with a torch scorer) that publishes `PrefillCandidateBlocks` per request and consumes them by gathering the kept blocks' dequantized K rows (`index_select` over `[2048 * 8]` rows per query row is the natural sparse path for torch) instead of scoring `[rows, lc]` and masking.
- Then `_publish_prefill_masks` / `cut_request_masks` / `CandidateMasks.request_masks` go away, and `enter_late_layer_tail` is the same on every platform.
- Keep the oracle property: the kernel tests (`test_dsv41_prefill_sparse_indexer.py`) compare implementations pairwise, so the torch one should stay the reference the others are checked against.

### 3. DeepGEMM sparse prefill under context parallelism

`make_candidate_indexer` gives the DeepGEMM indexer a `DenseCandidateIndexer` for prefill when `attn_cp_size > 1`, because a CP rank's local rows are interleaved across the prompt and `core.page_table[:num_tokens]` is not their page table. The consumers then pay the dense pass again (41 ms per layer at 262K).

- Build the per-row index page table from `req_to_token` (the way `slot_chunks` in `_low_ratio_index_topk_dense` already derives the slots: `req_to_token[req, j * ratio] // ratio`) so `PrefillIndexerInputs.kv_page_table` is CP-agnostic, then drop `prefill_dense`.
- Needs a CP run to validate; nothing in CI exercises DSv4.1 prefill CP with candidates today.

### 4. ROCm and the other backends

`DeepseekV4HipRadixBackend` (what `attention_registry.py` picks for `dsv4` on HIP) has no ratio-1/2 compressor / indexer path, so DSv4.1 does not run there yet; the Ascend backend has none either. When those land, the candidate indexer should be implemented against the protocol from the start rather than inline: `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` / the paged sparse kernel are CUDA-only (`_has_dense_fp4_indexer` checks `torch.version.cuda`), so the ROCm implementation would be aiter or Triton (the scorer of item 1 is the natural shared piece).

### 5. SM100 follow-ups inside the DeepGEMM implementation

Not backend coverage, but the remaining cost on the covered path:

- `get_paged_sparse_mqa_logits_metadata` is one 14 ms launch per chunk at 16384 rows (about 290 MB of schedule); all rows of a chunk share one page-table row, so a cheaper schedule for many rows of one request is the next win on the source side.
- The source's own top-512 and the block keys read every score tile twice (`TODO(dark)` in `candidate_indexer_deep_gemm.py`: one kernel for both).
- Verify rows: `publish_decode` pairs rows by `request_ids`; the prefill table uses the same path, but DSpark target-verify with candidates only has the `candidate_filtered` variant.

## Contract for a new implementation

- Prefill: `publish_prefill(inputs, out_positions)` writes the source layer's own top-k (flattened-K columns, `-1` padded, unordered) into `out_positions` and returns the published metadata; `select_prefill(published, inputs, out_positions)` writes a consumer's top-k in the same layout; `prefill_tail(published, tail_lens)` returns the metadata restricted to the last `tail_lens[b]` rows of each request. `PrefillIndexerInputs` carries the fp4 query, head weights, `compress_lens`, `request_starts`, rows and lengths per request, the flattened index K, the index-K pool view and the KV page table; `dense_prefill_indexer.score_tiles(inputs)` yields the dense scores tile by tile under #40217's budget for implementations that need them.
- Decode: `publish_decode(inputs, page_indices, raw_indices)` / `select_decode(published, inputs, page_indices, raw_indices)` over `IndexerInputs` (to be added to the ABC with item 1).
- Equivalence: the published blocks must equal `select_candidate_blocks` on the `-inf`-masked scores block for block; a consumer's selection must agree with `DenseCandidateIndexer.select_prefill` on the same inputs except at rounding-boundary ties (`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv41_prefill_sparse_indexer.py` is parametrizable over implementations); `test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer.py::TestCandidateIndexerGating` pins what `make_candidate_indexer` returns per platform.

### Related resources

_No response_

title: [Bug] DCP a2a backend NCCL crash at conc=64 (​unhandled cuda error​)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Two bugs prevent `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` from working at production concurrency and with `--enable-symm-mem`:

1. **NCCL crash (conc>32)**: `unhandled cuda error` in `pyncclGroupEnd` during eager decode (B > `cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`). Root cause: `_all_to_all_single` doesn't enable pynccl via `change_state(enable=True)`, falls back to `torch.distributed.all_to_all_single` which crashes on NCCL 2.27.7.
2. **OOM with `--enable-symm-mem`**: `prealloc_symmetric_memory_pool` allocates 4GB after `_profile_available_bytes` computes the KV cache budget, so the 4GB isn't accounted for → OOM at startup.

### Reproduction

* Start server with the above args
* Send 64+ concurrent requests (ISL=1024, OSL=1024)
* Server crashes during the first decode batch with `B > 32` (eager path)

### Environment

When using `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` with `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32` and `--max-running-requests 64`, the server crashes with `NCCL Error 1: unhandled cuda error` in `pyncclGroupEnd` during decode batches where `B > cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` (i.e., the eager decode path).

```
--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a
--attention-backend flashinfer --dtype bfloat16
--mem-fraction-static 0.88 --chunked-prefill-size 8192
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 --max-running-requests 64
```

title: [SM120] Field report: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in production on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (PCIe, no NVLink) - working config, measured throughput, rejected topologies
body:
## Summary

Field data from running **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** as a production SGLang backend on **8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe-only — no NVLink)**, including the *only* topology we could get to start, measured prefill/decode, a speculative-decoding A/B, and the configuration traps that cost us real experiments. Posting because SM120 + V4.1-Flash users currently have to rediscover all of this from scratch.

Full write-up (with methodology and reproduction artifacts): https://github.com/Lei-010/hermes-agent/blob/main/docs/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-SM120-Performance-and-Production-Config.md

Related: vLLM field report https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56700 (same hardware, vLLM side), vLLM https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56892 (SM120 bug/perf tracker).

## What works

```bash
docker run --gpus all -d --name dsv41 \
  --shm-size=64g --ipc=host --network host \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -e TP_SIZE=8 -e DP_SIZE=1 -e EP_SIZE=8 \
  -e SPEC_ALGORITHM=dspark -e DSPARK_BLOCK_SIZE=6 \
  -e CHUNKED_PREFILL_SIZE=2048 \
  -v /ssd/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:/model \
  <sglang image>
```

Effective `server_args` (verified at runtime via `/get_server_info`):

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `tp_size` / `ep_size` / `dp_size` | 8 / 8 / 1 |
| `speculative_algorithm` | DSPARK, `speculative_dspark_block_size = 6` |
| `chunked_prefill_size` | 2048 |
| `context_length` | 1,048,576 |
| `kv_cache_dtype` | `fp8_e4m3` |
| `mem_fraction_static` | 0.72 |
| `max_running_requests` | 16 |
| `attention_backend` / `moe_runner_backend` | `dsv4` / `flashinfer_mxfp4` |
| CUDA graph decode / prefill | full (max_bs 16) / **disabled** |

**TP8/EP8 is not a preference — it is the only layout that starts** (see "Topologies SGLang rejects" below).

## Measured throughput (cold, single stream, tokens from `usage`, not SSE chunk counts)

128K cold prefill:

| Config | tok/s |
|---|---|
| `chunked_prefill_size=2048` (production) | **6,853** |
| same config re-run | 6,765 (−1.3%) |
| flashmla prefill backend | 6,845 |
| fused-MoE all-reduce | 6,828 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=4096` | 6,301 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=1024` | 6,012 |

32K prompt: ≈7,196 tok/s. GPU util ≈87% at 220 W of 600 W → **communication-bound on PCIe**, not compute-bound. ~7K tok/s looks like the ceiling for this board without NVLink.

Radix/prefix cache is the only large multiplier: cache-hit prefill **0.34 s for a 112K-token prefix ≈ 325K tok/s (≈39×)**.

Decode (client path over SSH tunnel, production config): prose 93.9 tok/s, structured/JSON 134.1 tok/s, TTFT 143–169 ms.

## DSPARK A/B (block_size=2, clean legs, each verified via `server_info` + acceptance length)

| Prompt class | DSPARK ON | DSPARK OFF |
|---|---|---|
| prose | 76.5–78.9 tok/s | 36.4–36.5 tok/s |
| structured | 120.3–120.5 tok/s | 36.5 tok/s |
| `accept len` | 3.0 tokens/step | 1.0 |

With DSPARK off the model flattens to ~36.5 tok/s regardless of prompt class — speculation is the difference between usable and unusable latency on this hardware. Production ships `block_size=6` (structured ≈237–252 tok/s vs 120 at block 2).

## Traps that cost us experiments (SGLang-specific)

1. **`--enable-expert-parallel` is a vLLM flag** — SGLang takes `ep_size`; the vLLM spelling is rejected outright.
2. **`docker run` must pass `TP_SIZE`/`DP_SIZE`/`EP_SIZE` explicitly.** Without `-e`, the container silently serves TP8 defaults and your "new" config never happens (we recorded a full sweep of false data this way before adding a config gate).
3. **`ep_size ≤ tp_size`** or the MoE rank computation divides by zero: `moe_ep_rank = tp_rank % (tp_size // moe_dp_size) // (tp_size // moe_dp_size // ep_size)`.
4. **DSPARK + DP attention requires `--enable-dp-lm-head`** — but is unreachable on this model anyway (next section).

## Topologies SGLang rejects on this model

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| DP2 × TP4 (any EP) | `ValueError: V4.1 vision currently supports TP/EP without DP, CP, PP or MoE A2A` — both replicas die within ~70 s |
| prefill context-parallel | same class of rejection |
| `--enable-dp-attention` alone | silently no DP group (`dp_size: 1`) — looks fine, isn't |

Other SM120 gaps we hit: MSCCL++ (`_tune` kernel crash), FlashInfer all-reduce fusion, `flashmla_sparse_q8`, and CUDA-graph capture for **prefill** (crashes even with DSPARK off, i.e. unrelated to speculation).

## Operational notes

- A defunct container can survive a single `docker rm -f`; the next `docker run` then fails on the name conflict while an orphaned engine process keeps the port and answers health checks — which silently mislabels the next experiment. Loop `docker rm -f` until the container is gone **and** nothing listens on the port.
- A parse failure must never satisfy an "expected config" assertion, or a server that has not started yet gets recorded as "spec disabled".
- Verify intended config from the server (`/get_server_info`) before timing anything; discard legs that fail the gate rather than recording them.

## Not established

No 24 h soak (numbers come from a working day of production use), block sizes 4/8/12 not re-measured with the fixed sweep tool, and >32K prefill/long-context degradation not characterised.

title: [Performance] NVFP4 KV cache regresses Qwen4Exp decode ~29% on DGX Spark (SM121) vs fp8_e4m3 — consider arch-gating the default
body:
# [Performance] NVFP4 KV cache regresses Qwen4Exp decode ~29% on DGX Spark (SM121) vs fp8_e4m3

## Summary
`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` (the new default, `NVFP4_KV_CACHE=1`) costs **~29% single-stream
decode throughput** for Qwen4Exp-style models (QSA sparse attention) on GB10/SM121,
versus fp8_e4m3 KV. The FP4 packed-KV path's gather-side dequant is expensive on this
silicon; on datacenter parts the tradeoff may differ, but on Spark the pool-size win
is pointless (262K native context already fits with fp8) and the decode cost is real.

## Data (2× DGX Spark TP=2, NEXTN 3/1/4, decode CUDA graphs on, n=7-10 median)
| KV dtype | single-stream decode | notes |
|---|---|---|
| nvfp4 (default since the NVFP4-KV change) | 44.0 tok/s | also occasional deep dips |
| **fp8_e4m3** (`NVFP4_KV_CACHE=0`) | **56.8-58.6 tok/s** | stable |
| bf16 | 54-59 (more variance) | |

Same cluster, same weights (RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4), same bench
(`completion_tokens`-based streaming, 400-token runs).

## Suggestion
- Gate `NVFP4_KV_CACHE` default by arch: keep 1 on SM100+, default 0 on SM120/121 for
  QSA models (or autotune at first capture).
- Alternatively add a fused gather+dequant path for FP4 KV in the QSA Triton varlen
  fallback kernel (`qsa_fa_fallback.py` pattern used on SM121).

## Environment
Image lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38flashnext (+SM121 QSA fallback), 2×GB10, RoCEv2 TP2.
Full methodology: MiaAI-Lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Dual-DGX-Sparks → OPTIMIZATION-2026-08-28.md.

title: [DFLASH] Mamba state cache silently caps effective concurrency on hybrid-KDA models — 5 state slots/request, info-level log only (+75% throughput hidden behind one flag)
body:
## Summary
On hybrid linear-attention models (GLM-5.3-Flash: 34 KDA layers) with `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH`, each running request needs `1 + speculative_num_draft_tokens` mamba state slots. When the static-memory fraction is tight (large weights relative to VRAM — e.g. a 320B NVFP4 model on 2x DGX Spark), the derived `max_mamba_cache_size` can resolve far below `max_running_requests x (1+D)`, and the scheduler silently caps effective concurrency with only an info-level log line:

```
max_running_requests is capped to 2 by the mamba state cache (max_mamba_cache_size=10, 5 state slots per request).
```

Everything else still *looks* like an 8-stream server: `--max-running-requests 8` is accepted, `/get_server_info` reports 8, requests are admitted and queue. The throughput curve flattens at ~2 streams and is easy to misread as a hardware bandwidth ceiling. We shipped exactly that misreading in a published recipe before finding the log line.

## Measured impact (2x DGX Spark GB10, TP=2, GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 + DFlash2 drafter, D=5)
c-sweep, 12 distinct code prompts, 400 max_tokens, temp 0, stream:false, warmed, stock clocks:

| concurrency | capped (10 slots -> 2 streams) | fixed (40 slots) |
|---|---|---|
| c1 | 37.3 | 36.9 |
| c8 | 47.3 | **80.3** (8/8 concurrent) |
| c12 | 48.8 | **85.4** |

+75% aggregate at c12 from configuration alone. The fix on our rig:
`--max-mamba-cache-size 40 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --mem-fraction-static 0.90`
(bf16 ssm halves the per-slot cost, which is what makes 40 slots fit inside the fraction; measured cost ~6% single-stream decode from shorter accept lengths.)

## Suggestions (any one of these would have saved us a day)
1. When speculative decoding is enabled, derive the mamba cache floor from `max_running_requests x (1 + num_draft_tokens)` and fail loudly (or warn at WARNING level) if it cannot be met — same spirit as the existing draft-weights accounting in `_profile_available_bytes`.
2. Or: surface the effective cap in `/get_server_info` (e.g. `effective_max_running_requests`) so operators and load balancers can see the real ceiling.
3. Docs: a note in the speculative-decoding docs that hybrid-mamba models multiply state-slot cost by (1+D).

Happy to PR any of the three if maintainers have a preference. Full ladder and configs: https://github.com/beastllama/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2-SGLang-2x-DGX-Spark

Env: SGLang @ PR #36507 branch (aa8c950a3 base), 2x DGX Spark (GB10 sm_121, aarch64), CUDA 13, TP=2/nnodes=2.
Related: #36830 (fp8-KV on GB10), #36507 (GLM-5.3 support).

title: [Bug] Spec-v2 workers diverge on forward_batch_generation signature — 4 of 7 missing pp_proxy_tensors the scheduler always passes
body:
### Describe the bug

The scheduler's non-overlap speculative path always passes `pp_proxy_tensors` to the spec worker:

- `srt/managers/scheduler.py:4514` and `:4527` — `self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation(batch, pp_proxy_tensors=pp_proxy_tensors)`

But the spec-v2 workers have diverged on this signature. Audit of `python/sglang/srt/speculative/` on current `main`:

| Worker | `pp_proxy_tensors` |
|---|---|
| `eagle_worker_v2.py` | ✅ has it |
| `dflash_worker_v2.py` | ✅ has it |
| `ngram_worker.py` | ✅ has it |
| `dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py` | ❌ missing — reported in #39262 |
| `multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py` | ❌ missing — fixed inline in PR #29189 |
| `frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2.py` | ❌ missing — unreported |
| `uno_worker_v2.py` | ❌ missing — unreported |

Any model served through one of the four ❌ workers dies on the first scheduler step that takes this path with:

```
TypeError: <Worker>.forward_batch_generation() got an unexpected keyword argument 'pp_proxy_tensors'
```

Root cause: `BaseSpecWorker` (`srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py:154`) is an ABC but never declares `forward_batch_generation`, so nothing enforces the interface the scheduler calls through. Each worker evolved its own signature and three of them silently fell behind.

### Reproduction

See #39262 for a concrete DSpark repro (any configuration that forces the non-overlap path hits it on the first step). The same applies to the other three workers.

### Expected behavior / proposed fix

1. Add `pp_proxy_tensors=None` (and pass it through to the target worker) to `dspark_worker_v2.py`, `frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2.py`, and `uno_worker_v2.py` — same one-line shape as the `multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py` fix in #29189.
2. Declare `forward_batch_generation` on `BaseSpecWorker` (abstract method or a shared `Protocol`) so the next divergence fails at import/lint time instead of at the first request.

### Related

- #39262 — the DSpark instance of this bug
- #29189 — carries the `multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py` hunk as part of GigaChat 3.5 support
- #39885 — PP multi-layer EAGLE worker (separate `MultiLayerEagleWorkerPP` class); worth aligning on which component owns PP for multi-layer EAGLE before both land

title: [Bug][ROCm] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4_exp) crashes with HSAIL hardware exception 0x1016 on the first 16k prefill chunk, gfx950 TP1
body:
**Environment**: 1× MI350X (gfx950, VF), amdgpu 31.40/31.60, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260924`
(sglang 0.5.20.dev20260924+gce06a14444, torch 2.11+rocm7.2), model `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, context 262144.

**Command** (MI350X cookbook recipe adapted to TP1):
```
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --tp-size 1 \
  --attention-backend aiter --page-size 32 --kv-cache-dtype auto --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --context-length 262144 --max-running-requests 16 --trust-remote-code
```
Server starts ("fired up"); prompts of 122–465 tokens work; the first prefill chunk of 16384 tokens (a 32k prompt) aborts:
```
:0:rocdevice.cpp :3586: Callback: Queue ... aborting with error : HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION:
An HSAIL operation resulted in a hardware exception. code: 0x1016
Fatal Python error: Aborted
```
**What we tried** (each one server start + one 32k request):
| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| without MTP | crash |
| NEXTN 3/1/4 (MTP) | crash |
| `--attention-backend triton` | crash |
| `AITER_USE_NT=1` (MoE takes use_nt=False only at large M) | crash |
| `--chunked-prefill-size 8192` | crash |

| `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3 HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | **works** (prefill 17.7k tok/s, MTP accept ~3.0) |

Also: with a YaRN config (rope_type yarn on `text_config`), `Qwen4ExpConfig` copies `rope_parameters` to the top level and transformers'

Logs available (server logs for each variant).

title: [BUG] mxfp4 + sharded_state load format silently drops expert weights (gpt-oss-20b)
body:
## mxfp4 + `sharded_state` load format silently drops expert weights (gpt-oss-20b)

### Repro script

The script below loads `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, exports it with `save_sharded_state.py` (`--load-format sharded_state`), then compares the total size of the original checkpoint's safetensors against the exported ones. Run from the repo root:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

MODEL_PATH="${1:?usage: $0 /path/to/openai/gpt-oss-20b [out_dir]}"
OUT_DIR="${2:-$(mktemp -d -t mxfp4-repro-XXXXXX)}"

python3 -c "import sglang; print('sglang version:', sglang.__version__)"
SGLANG_ROOT=$(python3 -c "import os, sglang; print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(sglang.__file__))))")

python3 "${SGLANG_ROOT}/examples/runtime/engine/save_sharded_state.py" \
  --model-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \
  --attention-backend triton \
  --output "${OUT_DIR}"

echo "original checkpoint (safetensors only):"
du -ch "${MODEL_PATH}"/*.safetensors | tail -1
echo "sharded_state export (safetensors only):"
du -ch "${OUT_DIR}"/*.safetensors | tail -1
```

Run:

```
./repro_mxfp4_sharded_state_loss.sh /path/to/openai/gpt-oss-20b
```

### Result

Output (sglang 0.5.17, `lmsysorg/sglang:latest`, TP=2, GH200):

```
sglang version: 0.5.17
original checkpoint (safetensors only):
13G	total
sharded_state export (safetensors only):
4.0G	total
```

The export is missing every expert's packed FP4 weights (`w13_weight` / `w2_weight`); only the scales, biases, and everything else survive. Loading this checkpoint back with `--load-format sharded_state` runs every expert FFN on zeroed weights, with no error or warning.

### Problem source

This looks like a bug in sglang in the mxfp4 + `ShardedStateLoader` path.

**1. On quantization, the expert weights move off the module.** `Mxfp4MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` (triton_kernels branch, in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py`) moves the quantised weights to a helper object and then deletes them from `layer`, which is the `nn.Module`:

```python
self.w13_weight_triton_tensor = w13_weight
self.w2_weight_triton_tensor = w2_weight
del layer.w13_weight
del layer.w2_weight
```

**2. On save, `ShardedStateLoader.save_model` only sees what's still on the module.** It dumps `layer.state_dict()`, which by this point no longer contains `w13_weight` / `w2_weight`. They live on the quant-method helper object instead, which `state_dict()` never looks at.

**3. On load, the same deletion happens again, before the missing-key check can catch it.** `ShardedStateLoader.load_model` does:

```python
model = _initialize_model(...)
for _, module in model.named_modules():
    quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(module)
```

which zero-initializes the model before its missing-key check runs against it. The check is built from a `state_dict()` that's already missing `w13_weight` / `w2_weight`, so it never flags anything. The model loads "successfully" with those weights left at zero, with no error or warning.

title: [RFC] Backend, KV dtype and platform compatibility is checked case by case, and the responses are inconsistent
body:
### Motivation

While fixing #31346 I noticed that the bug I was fixing is one instance of a pattern, and that the project handles that pattern in at least four different ways depending on who wrote the code.

The concrete bug: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` together with `--dsa-decode-backend tilelang` is accepted on CUDA. The tilelang sparse kernel only has an fp8 path under ROCm, and on CUDA the kernel is compiled for bfloat16, so the server boots, loads the weights, and dies at decode CUDA-graph capture with `kernel main input KV dtype expected bfloat16, but got float8_e4m3fn`. I verified this on H100 at kernel level and on a DSA model across 4 nodes. The fix is three lines in argument resolution.

That fix is fine on its own. What bothers me is how it got there.

### The pattern

Constraints of the form "backend X only works on platform Y" or "backend X only supports kv-cache-dtype Z" are written by hand, one at a time, usually inside the PR that integrated the backend. `arg_groups/overrides.py` currently has 13 `raise ValueError` guards and `server_args.py` has 98 plus 101 asserts. Two of the DSA ones sit a few hundred lines below the guard I added and have exactly the same shape:

```python
if not is_blackwell_supported():
    raise ValueError("TRTLLM MLA backend is only supported on Blackwell GPUs (SM100/SM12x). Please use a different backend.")
if view.kv_cache_dtype not in ["fp8_e4m3", "fp4_e2m1", "bf16", "auto"]:
    raise ValueError("TensorRT-LLM MLA backend only supports kv-cache-dtype of fp8_e4m3, fp4_e2m1, bf16, or auto.")
```

Because each one is added independently, two things drift.

**The coverage is uneven.** In the DSA arm, of the 7 entries in `DSA_CHOICES` only 3 appear in any validation condition at all. `flashmla_sparse`, `flashmla_kv`, `flashmla_auto` and `trtllm` have none. This is awkward in my own case, because the error message I just added tells users to switch to `flashmla_kv` on Hopper or `trtllm` on Blackwell, and nothing checks that those accept what the user passes.

**The response is inconsistent.** Looking at merged PRs that deal with an unsupported combination, there are at least four different behaviours, all reasonable in isolation:

#23903 rejects the combination with an error. #31532 silently auto-disables one of the two features. #30463 keeps going and logs a warning. #23139 silently falls back to a different backend. #28689 is interesting because it was explicitly about deduplicating such asserts and filling one missing guard, which suggests I am not the first person to notice the shape.

From a user's point of view these are very different contracts. One tells you to fix your flags, one changes your configuration without asking, one changes it and mentions it in the log, and one changes it quietly. Today which of the four you get depends on which subsystem you happened to touch.

### Why it costs something

Because the check is missing rather than wrong, the failure surfaces late. In my case the server allocated the KV pool and reached decode CUDA-graph capture first, so on a multi-node deployment every attempt costs a full model load. Related reports look similar from the outside: #22277 is an fp8 KV dtype mismatch in Triton extend attention, #5700 is an fp8 KV cache producing nonsense output on fa3, #20163 is about incompatible KV layouts between trtllm and flashMLA.

### Prior work I found

#20481 refactored `server_args.py` and mentioned that each argument group could own its validation, but it was about code organisation rather than about whether the matrix is complete. #29630 is about the kernel namespace and notes in passing that backend coverage is hard to inspect. I did not find anything that treats the compatibility matrix itself as a thing to be filled in, so please point me at it if it exists.

### What I propose

Two steps, deliberately small, and the second one does not depend on the first.

**Step 1: fill one arm and see whether the shape holds.** Make the DSA compatibility matrix explicit as a declarative table living next to `_dsa_split_backend_resolution`, covering the 7 entries of `DSA_CHOICES` against the KV dtypes and platforms, with unit tests for every cell and hardware checks for the cells I can reach. Scope stays inside the DSA arm, nothing else changes, and it is easy to revert if the shape turns out to be wrong. The point of starting here is that the gaps are already known and I can verify them rather than guess.

**Step 2: write down which response is correct.** Independently of any table, agree on when an unsupported combination should raise, when it should auto-disable a feature, when it should fall back to another backend, and when a warning is enough. This costs almost nothing, it is a paragraph in the contribution guide plus review attention, and it stops the four behaviours above from multiplying further.

If step 1 works out, the natural continuation is to push the declarations from the table into the backends themselves, so each backend states its own platforms and dtypes and the resolver checks generically. I am deliberately not proposing that now: the DSA backends are plain strings in `DSA_CHOICES` dispatched through if/elif rather than registered objects, so doing it properly means introducing a registry first, and that is a much larger change than the problem currently justifies. Attention backends are in better shape for it, since they already have classes.

I also considered simply continuing to add guards by hand as gaps are found. That is the status quo, it is cheap per fix, and it needs no agreement from anyone, but the gaps keep being found by users in production and the inconsistent response stays. My own fix was found that way, which is what prompted this.

### What I am asking

Does this seem worth doing, or is case-by-case the deliberate choice here? If it is worth doing, is step 1 scoped the way you would want it, and does anyone object to starting in the DSA arm specifically? I am happy to write it, and I have hardware to verify the DSA cells on.

title: Weight Loader v2 — protocol and migration plan (PR1–PR6)
body:
# Weight Loader v2 — protocol and migration plan

Continuation of #24703. Foundation/reference path merged in #28671.

Audit basis: commit `3ebb7c2d0`. This plan includes native text loaders that fit the established dense/direct, standard-MoE or MLA protocols without adding a new shared loader abstraction. GLM-family loaders are isolated in a dedicated PR. Models requiring another protocol extension are explicitly not intended as part of this migration.

All migrations remain opt-in behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_WEIGHT_LOADER_V2` (default off).

---

## Protocol invariants

### Complete and explicit

Every checkpoint tensor entering v2 must be loaded, intentionally skipped by a named/tested rule, or rejected as unexpected. Missing targets, incomplete expert shards and pending fusion inputs must fail before execution. Broad exception fallback around parameter loaders is prohibited.

### Load first, derive second

1. Load and verify checkpoint tensors.
2. Run `post_load_weights` for derived buffers, absorbed MLA weights, merged views or kernel preparation.

Every loading path must run the same post-load contract exactly once.

### Parent migration includes affected downstream paths

Audit inheritance, `super()`, unbound parent calls, bound delegates, reward/classification/embedding heads, MTP/NextN/Eagle drafts, registry aliases and multimodal wrappers embedding a migrated text model.

- **Bound delegate:** automatically enters v2; require env-off/env-on routing smoke.
- **Unbound parent call:** unsafe; fix in the parent PR.
- **Inherit/super:** migrate or verify in the parent PR.
- **Manual wrapper:** remains independent; do not claim v2 coverage.

The regression fixed by #31988 is the minimum failure mode every parent PR must guard against.

### Required tests

- CPU mapping tests for every stacked/expert/remap rule;
- legacy-vs-v2 state-dict or logits equivalence;
- PP filtering and EP/expert-shard completeness where applicable;
- quantized checkpoint coverage for differing names/layouts;
- affected wrapper/delegate smoke in the same PR;
- no silent drop, duplicate post-load call or iterator double-consumption.

---

## Planned coverage

Denominator: **187** unique files under `python/sglang/srt/models/` defining at least one `load_weights`; `models/utils.py` is excluded.

- **PR1:** 2 files; cumulative **2/187 (1.1%)**.
- **PR2:** 69 files; cumulative **71/187 (38.0%)**.
- **PR3:** 8 files; cumulative **79/187 (42.2%)**.
- **PR4:** 4 files; cumulative **83/187 (44.4%)**.
- **PR5:** 3 files; cumulative **86/187 (46.0%)**.
- **PR6:** 6 files; cumulative **92/187 (49.2%)**.

Accounting: **92 planned + 95 not intended in this migration = 187**. Kimi K3 files are absent from the denominator commit.

---

## PR1 — merged reference path

- `llama.py`
- `qwen2.py`

### Downstream impact

- **PR2 debt:** `llama_classification.py`, `llama_reward.py`, `llama_embedding.py`, `llama_eagle.py`, `llama_eagle3.py`, `mistral.py`, `mistral_eagle.py`, `qwen2_classification.py`, `qwen2_rm.py`, `qwen2_eagle.py`.
- **Delegated multimodal smoke:** `llava.py`, `llavavid.py`, `voxtral.py`, `phi4mm.py`, `glmasr.py`, `points_v15_chat.py`, `nvila.py`, `nvila_lite.py`, `midashenglm.py`, `locate_anything.py`, `dots_ocr.py`, applicable `minicpmv.py` paths.
- **Manual multimodal, independent:** Qwen2 VL/audio and Qwen2 paths in InternVL/InternS1/MiniCPM wrappers.
- **No-loader aliases, smoke only:** `teleflm.py`, `llama4.py`, `ministral3.py`.

---

## PR2 — dense/direct and standard MoE

Only model-local stacked/expert mappings, remaps, named skips, PP filtering and existing parameter loaders are permitted. No new shared protocol extension belongs in this PR.

### Dense/direct — 30 files

- `gemma2.py`, `granite.py`, `internlm2.py`, `olmo.py`, `olmo2.py`, `qwen3.py`
- `apertus.py`, `arcee.py`, `baichuan.py`, `commandr.py`
- `exaone.py`, `exaone4.py`, `gemma.py`, `gpt_bigcode.py`, `gpt_j.py`
- `hrm_text.py`, `iquest_loopcoder.py`, `jet_nemotron.py`
- `mimo.py`, `mimo_mtp.py`, `minicpm.py`, `nemotron_nas.py`
- `orion.py`, `phi3_small.py`, `qwen.py`, `sdar.py`
- `solar.py`, `stablelm.py`, `starcoder2.py`, `xverse.py`

### Standard MoE — 23 files

- `mixtral.py`, `olmoe.py`, `phimoe.py`, `qwen2_moe.py`, `qwen3_moe.py`
- `afmoe.py`, `bailing_moe.py`, `cohere2_moe.py`, `dbrx.py`, `deepseek.py`
- `ernie4.py`, `ernie4_eagle.py`, `exaone_moe.py`, `exaone_moe_mtp.py`
- `hunyuan.py`, `hunyuan_v3.py`, `hunyuan_v3_nextn.py`
- `laguna.py`, `minimax_m2.py`, `minimax_m3.py`, `mixtral_quant.py`
- `sdar_moe.py`, `xverse_moe.py`

### Mandatory wrappers/delegates — 16 files

- `gemma2_reward.py`, `internlm2_reward.py`, `granitemoe.py`
- `qwen3_classification.py`, `qwen3_embedding.py`, `qwen3_moe_mtp.py`
- `llama_classification.py`, `llama_reward.py`, `llama_embedding.py`
- `llama_eagle.py`, `llama_eagle3.py`, `mistral.py`, `mistral_eagle.py`
- `qwen2_classification.py`, `qwen2_rm.py`, `qwen2_eagle.py`

`qwen3_rm.py` has no own `load_weights`; it requires smoke but does not affect coverage.

### Deliverables

- `StackedParamsDispatch` and `ExpertParamsDispatch`;
- model-local aliases/remaps and named skips;
- PP filtering, tied-head behavior and required expert-shard completeness;
- wrapper preprocessing preserved before delegation;
- mapping matrices, wrapper smoke and dense/MoE equivalence.

### Downstream impact

- **Unbound—must fix:** Gemma2/InternLM2 reward, GraniteMoe and PR1 classification/reward/Eagle paths.
- **Inherit/super:** Qwen3-MoE MTP, Ernie Eagle, Exaone MTP, Hunyuan NextN and MiMo MTP.
- **No-loader smoke:** `mellum.py`, `qwen3_rm.py` and PR1 aliases.
- **Multimodal smoke:** applicable Cohere, Ernie, Gemma, Jet, Qwen, MiniCPM, SDAR and Xverse downstream wrappers; full towers remain outside coverage.

---

## PR3 — MLA fusion and post-load derivation

### Scope — 8 files

- `deepseek_v2.py`
- `deepseek_nextn.py`
- `mistral_large_3.py`
- `kimi_k25_eagle3.py`
- `longcat_flash.py`
- `longcat_flash_nextn.py`
- `minicpm3.py`
- `sarvam_moe.py`
- helper: `deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py` (not in denominator)

### Deliverables

- conditional shared-expert remap;
- explicit multi-input MLA fusion with pending-input verification;
- kv/FP8 remaps, PP/NextN filtering and exactly-once post-load derivation;
- async/stream-safe loading;
- fusion on/off, NextN, truncated/PP and equivalence tests.

### Downstream impact

- **Inherit/super:** DeepSeek NextN, Mistral Large 3 and `mistral_large_3_eagle.py` smoke.
- **Delegated multimodal smoke:** `deepseek_vl2.py`, `dots_vlm.py`, `kimi_k25.py`; verify stripped names, iterator ownership and post-load once.
- **Manual multimodal, independent:** `kimi_vl.py`, `deepseek_ocr.py`.
- LongCat and NextN migrate together. Kimi K2.5/Eagle3 is not Kimi K3.

---

## PR4 — Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next language paths

No additional model is added to PR4.

- `qwen3_5.py`
- `qwen3_next.py`
- `qwen3_5_mtp.py`
- `qwen3_next_mtp.py`

### Deliverables

- packed GDN and fused-expert dispatch;
- standard/shared-expert MoE and hybrid mixer loading for these Qwen families;
- MTP parity and strict text/vision key separation;
- dense/MoE, GDN, fused-expert and MTP equivalence/smoke tests.

### Downstream impact

- MiniCPM-V 4.6 text delegation requires smoke.
- Qwen3.5 conditional-generation classes remain manual multimodal paths.
- `interns2preview.py` requires smoke if the conditional loader changes.

---

## PR5 — DeepSeek V4 only

- `deepseek_v4.py`
- `deepseek_v4_nextn.py`
- `deepseek_v4_dspark.py`

No additional model was confirmed to share V4 compressor/`wo_a` semantics.

### Downstream impact

- NextN must preserve filtering and exactly-once post-load.
- DSPARK must preserve its draft path while sharing PR5 mappings.
- No additional downstream multimodal entry class was identified at `3ebb7c2d0`.

---

## PR6 — GLM family

GLM is isolated because one file can expose standard GLM loading while another entry class inherits the PR3 DeepSeek/MLA path. This PR depends on PR2 and PR3.

### Scope — 6 files

- `chatglm.py`
- `glm4.py`
- `glm4_moe.py`
- `glm4_moe_nextn.py`
- `glm4_moe_lite.py`
- `glm4_moe_lite_nextn.py`

### Deliverables

- ChatGLM version/prefix normalization and checked fused-QKV layout;
- GLM4 dense mappings and PP/tied-head behavior;
- GLM4-MoE shared-expert remap, expert completeness and NextN filtering;
- GLM4-MoE-Lite MLA reuse from PR3;
- DSA entry-class inheritance smoke across PR3 and PR6;
- family-wide env-off/env-on equivalence.

### Downstream impact

- `glm4v.py`, `glm4v_moe.py`, `glm_ocr.py`, `glm_ocr_nextn.py`, `glm_image_vl.py`, `glmasr.py` and `midashenglm.py` require routing smoke where they embed, inherit or manually duplicate a GLM text path.
- Full vision/OCR/audio tower loading remains outside coverage.

---

## Not intended in this migration

### Native text loaders requiring another protocol or separate acceptance — 28 files

- `opt.py` — one-source tensor fanout/TP reconstruction requires a transform/fanout protocol.
- `grok.py` — output multiplier conversion requires checked tensor transforms.
- `llada2.py` — lm-head normalization requires a value-transform hook.
- `dflash.py` — speculative draft-only loader requires separate draft acceptance.
- `dspark.py` — one-shot backbone/Markov/confidence routing requires a stream router and mergeable results.
- `gemma3_causal.py` — embedding variant requires a declared auxiliary checkpoint-source protocol.
- `gpt2.py` — Conv1D transpose requires checked tensor transforms.
- `persimmon.py` — reshape/transpose requires checked tensor transforms.
- `phi.py` — packed checkpoint fanout requires transform/fanout dispatch.
- `torch_native_llama.py` — alternate nested module tree requires recursive prefix dispatch and completeness accounting.
- `bailing_moe_linear.py`, `bailing_moe_nextn.py` — linear-attention routing requires a generic hybrid mixer protocol.
- `falcon_h1.py` — Mamba/convolution loading requires a hybrid mixer protocol.
- `gemma3n_causal.py` — nonstandard per-layer projections require hybrid dispatch.
- `kimi_linear.py` — KDA packing plus MLA derivation requires hybrid dispatch composed with PR3.
- `lfm2.py`, `lfm2_moe.py` — short-convolution and batched experts require hybrid and batched-expert dispatch.
- `nemotron_h.py`, `nemotron_h_mtp.py` — Mamba state/convolution plus MTP requires hybrid dispatch.
- `gemma4_causal.py`, `gemma4_mtp.py` — batched expert tensors/scales require batched-expert dispatch.
- `granitemoehybrid.py` — hybrid routing and combined expert tensors require hybrid plus batched-expert dispatch.
- `step3p5.py`, `step3p5_mtp.py` — batched experts/shared slots require batched-expert dispatch.
- `zaya.py` — fused experts and persistent CCA/balancing buffers require fanout and buffer-target accounting.
- `gpt_oss.py` — MXFP4/Quark layouts and deferred scales require quant-layout dispatch.
- `mimo_v2.py`, `mimo_v2_nextn.py` — TP resharding, packed QKV, DeepEP experts and auxiliary routing require multiple new protocols.

### Explicit model exclusion

- **Kimi K3 only:** `kimi_k3.py`, `kimi_k3_vl.py` — implementation/checkpoint contract is absent from the audited `main` commit; zero denominator files.

### Full multimodal/OCR/vision — 53 files

Cause: each file owns or interleaves a full tower loader. Bound text delegates still receive parent-PR smoke.

- `cohere2_vision.py`, `deepseek_janus_pro.py`, `deepseek_ocr.py`, `deepseek_vl2.py`, `dots_ocr.py`, `dots_vlm.py`, `ernie45_vl.py`
- `gemma3_mm.py`, `gemma3n_mm.py`, `gemma4_mm.py`, `gemma4_unified.py`
- `glm4v.py`, `glm4v_moe.py`, `glm_image_vl.py`, `glm_ocr.py`, `glm_ocr_nextn.py`
- `inkling.py`, `interns1.py`, `interns1pro.py`, `internvl.py`, `jet_vlm.py`
- `kimi_k25.py`, `kimi_vl.py`, `lfm2_vl.py`, `lightonocr.py`, `llava.py`, `llavavid.py`, `locate_anything.py`, `midashenglm.py`
- `minicpmo.py`, `minicpmv.py`, `minimax_m3_vl.py`, `mllama.py`, `mllama4.py`, `moss_vl.py`, `nano_nemotron_vl.py`, `nvila.py`, `nvila_lite.py`
- `paddleocr_vl.py`, `phi4mm.py`, `pixtral.py`, `points_v15_chat.py`
- `qwen2_5_vl.py`, `qwen2_vl.py`, `qwen3_omni_moe.py`, `qwen3_vl.py`, `qwen3_vl_moe.py`
- `sarashina2_vision.py`, `step3_vl.py`, `step3_vl_10b.py`, `step3p7.py`, `unlimited_ocr.py`, `yivl.py`

### Speech/audio-specific — 7 files

Cause: audio encoder/decoder contracts and tests are required.

- `glmasr.py`, `mimo_v2_asr.py`, `parakeet.py`, `qwen2_audio.py`, `qwen3_asr.py`, `voxtral.py`, `whisper.py`

### Encoder-only — 5 files

Cause: encoder/classification loading requires a separate acceptance protocol.

- `bert.py`, `clip.py`, `radio.py`, `roberta.py`, `siglip2.py`

### Backend adapters — 2 files

Cause: framework adapters are not native model-family migrations.

- `mindspore.py`, `transformers.py`

---

## Dependencies and merge order

```text
PR1 merged
  └─ PR2 dense/direct + standard MoE + wrappers
       ├─ PR3 MLA + wrappers
       └─ PR4 Qwen3.5/Qwen3-Next + wrappers

PR5 DeepSeek V4
  └─ follows stabilization of PR3 post-load/MLA contracts

PR6 GLM family
  └─ depends on PR2 standard dispatch and PR3 MLA/DSA behavior
```

---
