title: [Bug]  --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave crashes on DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 (v0.5.16)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

In SGLang v0.5.16 (cu129 Docker image), the newly unified context parallelism parameters --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave crash on startup with a ValueError when used with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8.

Per the [PR](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27312) and cookbook, --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave is the intended unified CLI design meant to replace the old fragmented parameter set (--enable-nsa-prefill-context-parallel, --nsa-prefill-cp-mode, etc.). However, in v0.5.16, the unified parameters fail during argument validation, while the old-style parameters work as a workaround.

title: [Bug] [MLX] Hunyuan cannot be served: auto_map fails in kv_cache_builder.resolve_transformers_arch
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.

## Describe the bug

On the MLX backend (`SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`), serving `mlx-community/Hunyuan-7B-Instruct-4bit` (and any Hunyuan model whose HF config ships an `auto_map` to `modeling_hunyuan.py`) crashes during scheduler initialization, **after** the MLX model itself has loaded successfully through `mlx_lm.load`.

This is separate from the `dp_size` startup crash fixed in #32520 — it only surfaces once that one is applied.

## Reproduction

```bash
SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path mlx-community/Hunyuan-7B-Instruct-4bit \
  --trust-remote-code --tp-size 1 --disable-radix-cache --disable-cuda-graph \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 --max-running-requests 1 --context-length 2048
```

## Error

```
[transformers] Failed to load dynamic modules from auto_map for 'HunYuanForCausalLM':
  module 'transformers_modules.mlx_hyphen_community.Hunyuan_hyphen_7B_hyphen_Instruct_hyphen_4bit....modeling_hunyuan'
  has no attribute 'HunyuanModel'. Skipping remote model compatibility checks.

  File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py", line 151, in build_kv_cache
    get_resolved_model_impl(model_config) == ModelImpl.TRANSFORMERS
  File ".../sglang/srt/model_loader/utils.py", line 245, in get_resolved_model_impl
    _, resolved_arch = get_model_architecture(model_config)
  File ".../sglang/srt/model_loader/utils.py", line 227, in get_model_architecture
    architectures = resolve_transformers_arch(model_config, architectures)
  File ".../sglang/srt/model_loader/utils.py", line 160, in resolve_transformers_arch
    raise ValueError(...)
ValueError: Cannot find model module. 'HunYuanForCausalLM' is not a registered model in the Transformers library
and loading the custom model from auto_map failed.
```

The MLX model loads fine before this point:
```
[...] MLX model loaded in 2.12s
[...] Wired memory limit set to 51.8 GB
[...] Auto-sized attention KV pool: ... pool_size=49940
[...] MLX stub: initialized minimal pools (max_total_num_tokens=45439, max_running_requests=1, ...)
```

## Root cause (initial analysis)

On the MLX path the model is loaded via `mlx_lm.load()`, so `sglang/srt/models/*` and the HF `auto_map` are never needed for inference. But `kv_cache_builder.build_kv_cache` still calls `get_resolved_model_impl(model_config)` → `get_model_architecture` → `resolve_transformers_arch`, which tries to import the `auto_map` module and fails because `modeling_hunyuan.py` does not expose the class name SGLang expects (`HunyuanModel`).

This looks analogous to the `init_attention_backends()` no-op override added to the MLX stub in #30050 to skip a CUDA-only path: the MLX path likely needs to short-circuit the transformers-architecture resolution in `kv_cache_builder` as well (the MLX backend does not route inference through `sglang/srt/models`).

Models without a remote `auto_map` (e.g. the qwen2_moe / qwen3_moe repos used by the existing MLX correctness tests) do not hit this, which is why it stayed hidden.

## Environment

```
sglang: main @ 08af5ae (with #32520 applied)
mlx: 0.32.0, mlx-lm: 0.31.3, mlx-metal: 0.32.0
torch: 2.11.0, transformers: 5.12.1
macOS: 15.7, Apple M2 Max (64 GB)
Model: mlx-community/Hunyuan-7B-Instruct-4bit (architectures: ['HunYuanForCausalLM'], model_type: hunyuan)
```

## Context

Blocks the `hunyuan.py` item on the Apple Silicon roadmap (#19137, "Model Support"). `mlx_lm` already ships a `hunyuan` implementation (both MoE `hunyuan.py` and dense `hunyuan_v1_dense.py`), so once this integration gap is closed the Hunyuan MLX correctness test can land.

cc @yeahdongcn @jonahbernard @jlee5814

title: [Bug]  CPU OffloaderV2 with DeepEP fails when local expert count is not in copy_to_gpu_no_ce supported sizes
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Environment

- Model: GLM-5.2 FP8
- `n_routed_experts=256`
- `--ep-size 16`
- DeepEP normal mode
- CPU OffloaderV2:

```bash
--offload-group-size 4 \
--offload-num-in-group 1 \
--offload-prefetch-step 1
```

## Problem

Enabling CPU OffloaderV2 causes Prefill warmup to fail with:

```
RuntimeError: unexpected N
```

The failure occurs in:

```
sglang.srt.layers.moe.moe_runner.deep_gemm
    -> copy_list_to_gpu_no_ce()
    -> sgl_kernel.copy_to_gpu_no_ce()
```

Relevant code:

```python
if get_offloader().forbid_copy_engine_usage:
    num_recv_tokens_per_expert_gpu = copy_list_to_gpu_no_ce(
        num_recv_tokens_per_expert
    )
```

When CPU OffloaderV2 is enabled, `forbid_copy_engine_usage` is `true`, so this path is taken unconditionally.

## Root Cause

`num_recv_tokens_per_expert` is a small `int32` control vector produced after DeepEP dispatch. It contains the number of received tokens for every local expert and is used by `ep_scatter()` / grouped GEMM to compute per-expert offsets and work sizes.

For this configuration:

```
global routed experts: 256
EP size:               16
local experts/rank:    16
```

Therefore, the control vector has:

```
N = 16
```

However, the installed `sgl_kernel.copy_to_gpu_no_ce` only provides fixed-size specializations for:

```
N = 32, 64, 72
```

```cpp
void copy_to_gpu_no_ce(const at::Tensor& input, at::Tensor& output) {
  int N = static_cast<int>(input.numel());
  if (N == 72) {
    copy_to_gpu_no_ce_impl<72>(input, output);
  } else if (N == 64) {
    copy_to_gpu_no_ce_impl<64>(input, output);
  } else if (N == 32) {
    copy_to_gpu_no_ce_impl<32>(input, output);
  } else {
    TORCH_CHECK(false, "unexpected N");
  }
}
```

It does not support `N=16`, which causes:

```
RuntimeError: unexpected N
```

This is not an invalid DeepEP output.

`N=16` is the expected local expert count for:

```
256 experts / EP16
```

## Expected Behavior

CPU OffloaderV2 should work with DeepEP for arbitrary valid local expert counts, including `N=16`.

## Actual Behavior

The service fails during model warmup / first Prefill forward:

```
File "sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py", line ...
    num_recv_tokens_per_expert_gpu = copy_list_to_gpu_no_ce(...)

File "sgl_kernel/elementwise.py", line 420
    torch.ops.sgl_kernel.copy_to_gpu_no_ce(input, output)

RuntimeError: unexpected N
```

## Suggested Fix

Avoid calling the fixed-shape kernel unconditionally.

### Option A: Add a generic fallback

```python
if len(num_recv_tokens_per_expert) in SUPPORTED_NO_CE_SIZES:
    use copy_to_gpu_no_ce(...)
else:
    use pinned CPU tensor.cuda(non_blocking=True)
```

### Option B: Fallback permanently after unsupported size

Catch the unsupported-size error once and permanently fall back to the regular pinned-memory H2D path for the process.

### Option C: Add an `N=16` specialization

Add a dedicated `N=16` implementation to `copy_to_gpu_no_ce`.

Option A/B is more robust because future models may use different expert counts and EP configurations.

## Workaround

Use the normal pinned-memory H2D copy path for unsupported `N`.

This does not change:

- DeepEP routing
- token counts
- expert offsets
- grouped GEMM semantics

It only disables the `copy_to_gpu_no_ce` optimization for this small control vector.

### Reproduction

## Cross-machine CP Note

This reproduction intentionally enables experimental cross-machine context
parallelism:

```bash
export SGLANG_ALLOW_CROSS_MACHINE_CP=1
```

By default, SGLang rejects cross-machine CP when `tp_size > 8`. The current
source gates this configuration behind `SGLANG_ALLOW_CROSS_MACHINE_CP`, rather
than enabling it silently.

The failure in this issue is independent of that experimental CP gate:

- Cross-machine TP16/CP16 distributed initialization succeeds.
- Mooncake RDMA initialization succeeds.
- Model weights load successfully.
- The failure occurs later, during the first Prefill warmup forward in:
  `copy_to_gpu_no_ce(num_recv_tokens_per_expert)`.

- The same cross-machine CP16 configuration starts successfully when
  OffloaderV2 is disabled.


## Full Command

```bash
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0
export NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5_3,mlx5_4,mlx5_5,mlx5_6,mlx5_8,mlx5_9,mlx5_10,mlx5_11
export NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX=2
export NCCL_IB_ROCE_VERSION_NUM=1

export MC_GID_INDEX=3
export PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sglang/python
export SGLANG_ALLOW_CROSS_MACHINE_CP=1
export SGLANG_RUN_ID=glm52-prefill-offload-v2

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/public/modellist/452/V1 \
  --tp-size 16 \
  --ep-size 16 \
  --nnodes 2 \
  --node-rank `<0-or-1>` \
  --dist-init-addr 192.168.4.3:20001 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.82 \
  --disaggregation-mode prefill \
  --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake \
  --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_bond_0 \
  --enable-prefill-cp \
  --cp-strategy interleave \
  --enable-dsa-cache-layer-split \
  --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --deepep-mode normal \
  --disable-cuda-graph \
  --offload-group-size 4 \
  --offload-num-in-group 1 \
  --offload-prefetch-step 1
```

title: [Bug] KV metrics report token capacity as block capacity when `page_size > 1`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

# [Bug] KV metrics report token capacity as block capacity when `page_size > 1`

## Description

`KvMetrics.kv_total_blocks` and `KvMetrics.kv_active_blocks` are currently
reported in token units, despite their names indicating block/page units.

Current code:

```python
kv_metrics.kv_active_blocks = int(
    self.get_stats().token_usage * self.max_total_num_tokens
)
kv_metrics.kv_total_blocks = self.max_total_num_tokens
```

However, `max_total_num_tokens` is a token capacity. Elsewhere, SGLang
derives the number of KV pages as:

```python
num_pages = self.max_total_num_tokens // self.page_size
```

Therefore, when `page_size > 1`, both `kv_*_blocks` values are reported in
tokens rather than blocks/pages. Their values are over-reported by
approximately `page_size` times. The issue is hidden when `page_size == 1`.

## Expected behavior

`kv_total_blocks` should report the KV page/block count:

```python
num_blocks = self.max_total_num_tokens // self.page_size
kv_metrics.kv_total_blocks = num_blocks
```

`kv_active_blocks` should use the same unit:

```python
kv_metrics.kv_active_blocks = int(
    self.get_stats().token_usage * num_blocks
)
```

## Example

With:

- `max_total_num_tokens = 8192`
- `page_size = 16`
- `token_usage = 0.5`

The current metrics report:

- `kv_total_blocks = 8192`
- `kv_active_blocks = 4096`

Expected block/page metrics should be:

- `kv_total_blocks = 512`
- `kv_active_blocks = 256`

## Suggested test

Add a unit test with `page_size > 1` (for example, `16`) to verify that
`kv_total_blocks == max_total_num_tokens // page_size`, while retaining a
`page_size == 1` case for backward compatibility.

## Relevant code

- Metrics assignment: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/kv_events_publisher.py#L83-L91
- Page count calculation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L977-L983

title: [Bug] Text-only requests on a multimodal-capable checkpoint pay two extra full-context tokenizations (rising TTFT floor on long conversations)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] Please use English.

### Describe the bug

Both `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions` decide how to hand the prompt to
the engine by looking only at `model_config.is_multimodal`, which says the
*checkpoint* can accept media — not that *this request* carries any:

`python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_responses.py` (current `main`, 4ea17169b):

```python
is_multimodal = self.tokenizer_manager.model_config.is_multimodal
processed_messages = self._process_messages(chat_request, is_multimodal)

if is_multimodal:
    request_prompts = [processed_messages.prompt]      # text
    engine_prompts = [processed_messages.prompt]
else:
    request_prompts = [processed_messages.prompt_ids]  # ids
    engine_prompts = [processed_messages.prompt_ids]
```

`serving_chat.py` has the same shape (`elif is_multimodal: prompt_kwargs = {"text": ...}`).

So a **text-only request served by a multimodal-capable checkpoint** throws away
the `prompt_ids` that `_process_messages` just produced and passes a string.
Downstream this costs two extra full-context tokenizations per request:

1. `serving_responses.py` re-encodes the prompt to compute the output budget:
   `prompt_length = len(tokenizer.encode(engine_prompt))` (~line 293), only
   reached because `engine_prompt` is now a `str`;
2. `TokenizerManager._tokenize_one_request` encodes the same text again before
   scheduling.

Both are O(context). On short prompts this is invisible. On **long, append-only
conversations** (agent / tool-calling traffic, where each turn resends the whole
history) it grows every turn and shows up as a steadily rising TTFT floor even
when only a few hundred new tokens are appended.

### Evidence

Qwen3.5-122B (image-capable checkpoint) driven by pure-text agent traffic,
TP4, 262144 context, prefix cache warm:

- Per-request first-byte floor scales ~2.7x with total context; late-session
  requests take >1s to first byte while appending only ~500 new tokens.
- Same boot, comparable context: `chat` 0.60s vs `responses` 1.76s — i.e. ~1.16s
  of the responses-path latency is this extra work.
- `py-spy` on the API process: **~80% of CPU in `_encode_plus`**, split roughly
  in thirds across the shared template encode, the `create_responses` length
  budget encode, and the generate path encode.
- `SGLANG_INCREMENTAL_TOKENIZE=1` only recovers the shared-template third
  (1.76s -> 1.45s); the other two bypass the cache because they re-encode text.

### Fix

Gate the text path on whether the request actually carries media
(`image_data` / `video_data` / `audio_data` on `MessageProcessingResult`).
Requests with media keep the exact previous behaviour (including the Inkling
pre-rendered-ids branch); text-only requests keep their token ids. The
`prompt_ids is str` corner case still falls back to the text path explicitly.

Measured after the change, late-session warm requests at ~100k context:

| path | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `/v1/responses` | 1.72s | **0.88s (-49%)** |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | 0.49s | **0.27s (-45%)** |

A 20-request in-order replay of a real long session reproduces it
(1.73s -> 0.96s average, -45%); early short-context requests show no regression.
With incremental tokenization additionally enabled the responses floor reaches
0.51s (-70% cumulative), matching the chat path.

### Related

- #29287 — same `prompt_length` computation, other direction: for requests that
  *do* carry images the pre-expansion count under-counts and can produce a 400.
  Complementary; this issue is about text-only requests never needing that
  encode at all.
- #17206 (open, stale) — removes the encode -> decode round-trip inside
  `_apply_jinja_template` for multimodal models. Complementary: it makes the
  text path cheaper to produce, this makes text-only requests not take it.
- #27298 — also targets the jinja-path encode/decode round-trip.

### Environment

SGLang `main` @ 4ea17169b, CUDA 13.0, 4x GPU TP4, Qwen3.5-122B-A3B,
`--context-length 262144`, radix cache on. Client: pure-text OpenAI Responses
traffic from a coding agent (no image/audio/video parts in any request).

title: [Bug] Object-store speculative draft metadata is not downloaded before worker startup
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] This report includes environment information and a minimal reproduction.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general discussion question.
- [x] This issue is written in English.

### Describe the bug

When the target and speculative draft models use different S3-compatible object-storage paths, SGLang downloads metadata only for the target model and tokenizer during `ServerArgs` post-processing. The draft path is not prepared by `ObjectStorageModel.download_and_get_path()` before the draft worker constructs its `ModelConfig`.

This leaves the draft metadata cache without files such as `config.json` and `model.safetensors.index.json`. Even when the draft load format is correctly selected as `runai_streamer`, configuration or shard-index access can fail or fall through to behavior intended for a local/Hugging Face path.

The draft object-storage path should have its non-weight metadata downloaded before workers are launched. If the draft and target paths are identical, the metadata should be downloaded only once.

This is separate from #32202: that issue covers resolving an explicit draft `auto` load format to the correct loader. This issue covers preparing the draft metadata after an object-storage loader is selected, including when `runai_streamer` is specified explicitly.

### Reproduction

Launch speculative decoding with separate target and draft paths in S3-compatible object storage:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path s3://bucket/target-model \
  --load-format runai_streamer \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-draft-model-path s3://bucket/draft-model \
  --speculative-draft-load-format runai_streamer
```

Before worker initialization, observe that `ServerArgs._handle_model_source_paths()` calls `ObjectStorageModel.download_and_get_path()` for the target path, but not for the distinct draft path. The draft `ModelConfig` later resolves its local metadata directory with `ObjectStorageModel.get_path()` even though that cache was never populated.

### Environment

- SGLang: latest `origin/main`, commit `5cc273a780`
- Model storage: S3-compatible object storage
- Deployment where observed: 2 nodes, TP=8, PP=2, NVIDIA H20
- The failure occurs during draft configuration/weight preparation before model execution.

title: [Feature] Select only required RunAI shards for MTP draft models
body:
### Checklist

- [x] This is a feature request, not a general discussion question.
- [x] This issue is written in English.

### Motivation

`RunaiModelStreamerLoader` currently passes every safetensors shard to RunAI when loading an MTP/NextN speculative draft model. Draft tensor filtering happens only after `runai_safetensors_weights_iterator()` has opened the shards and started producing tensors.

For a large sharded target checkpoint with bundled draft weights, the draft worker therefore scans and opens all target-model shards even though it needs only one requested MTP layer and draft-wide shared parameters. With object storage this also causes unnecessary remote header reads and increases startup I/O and file-descriptor pressure.

SGLang already downloads `model.safetensors.index.json` into the object-storage metadata cache before worker startup. The RunAI loader should use that index to select the shards containing the requested draft layer before constructing the RunAI iterator.

The selection should support checkpoint layouts seen in practice:

- Native DeepSeek keys such as `mtp.<index>.*`.
- Hugging Face-style keys such as `model.mtp.layers.<index>.*`.
- Draft-wide parameters under the MTP namespace that are required by every draft layer.

If the index is missing, malformed, or uses an unknown layout, loading should safely fall back to all shards.

### Related resources

- RunAI Model Streamer loader: `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py`
- Safetensors shard mapping: `model.safetensors.index.json`
- Related object-storage draft metadata preparation is tracked separately because it applies before shard selection.

title: [Bug] Prefill input logprobs are served from the wrong request when a batch member is retracted or finished
body:
### Describe the bug

In `process_batch_result_prefill`, the branch that skips finished-in-a-mixed-batch and retracted requests does not advance `logprob_pt`, so every later request in the same batch reads a shifted slice of the flat input-logprob array and is served **another request's prompt logprobs**.

The flat array holds one block per request in batch order regardless of whether that request asked for logprobs. That is why `_apply_prefill_logprobs` advances the cursor outside its `return_logprob` guard ([`batch_result_processor.py:522`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py#L522)):

```python
        if req.return_logprob:
            self.logprob_result_processor.add_logprob_return_values(...)
        logprob_pt += num_input_logprobs
        return logprob_pt
```

The producer agrees: `logits_processor.py` builds `extend_logprob_pruned_lens_cpu` by appending `extend_len - start_len` for every sequence in the batch, using the same formula the consumer uses in `calculate_num_input_logprobs`.

But the skip at [`batch_result_processor.py:307-313`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py#L307-L313) steps over a request without stepping the cursor:

```python
                if (
                    req.finished() and req.inflight_middle_chunks <= 0
                ) or req.is_retracted:
                    # Decode req in a mixed batch, or a retracted req. Keep an
                    # aborted middle chunk in the chunked branch long enough to
                    # drain its accounting without streaming it.
                    continue
```

`logprob_pt` is initialized at line 286 and advanced only at lines 344 and 374, both after this `continue`.

Nothing raises. The assertion in `logprob_result_processor.py` checks the slice **length**, not its offset, and the shift is always backwards, so it never runs off the end. The diagnostic signature is that `input_top_logprobs_val[i]` is indexed per request and stays correct while `input_token_logprobs` is sliced by the cursor and is wrong.

The disaggregated prefill loop already handles exactly this. `disaggregation/prefill.py:703` defines `advance_logprob_pt()` and calls it on each of its skip paths at lines 721, 789 and 797.

Scope: this bites when the skipped request itself requested input logprobs (`logprob_start_len >= 0`). With the default `-1` its block is zero rows and the skip is harmless. Overlap scheduling is on by default and retraction is ordinary under KV pressure, so no unusual flag is required.

### Reproduction

Driving the real `process_batch_result_prefill` on CPU with two prefill requests, the first retracted, `extend_input_len_per_req=[2, 3]` and `extend_logprob_start_len_per_req=[0, 0]`, over a flat array of `[-1.0, -2.0, -30.0, -31.0, -32.0]`:

```
expected (active request's own block)  [None, -30.0, -31.0]
actual                                 [None,  -1.0,  -2.0]   <- the retracted request's values
```

I have a regression test that reproduces this, written against the existing `test_batch_result_processor_hidden_states.py` harness and registered as `register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")`, so it needs no GPU. It fails on `main` and passes with the cursor advanced. I will open a PR with the fix and that test shortly and link it here.

Related but distinct, so neither covers this path:
- [#34153](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34153) applies the same "consume the slice, skip the attach" idea to the `req.to_finish` path, which routes through the normal branch rather than this skip.
- [#36724](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36724) adds a new `deferred_mm_abort` branch immediately above this `continue` and advances the cursor there, leaving this one unchanged.
- [#32103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32103) and [#32089](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32089) describe the hidden-states analog and both cite this logprob path as already correct.

### Environment

`python3 -m sglang.check_env` does not run on a CPU-only host. [`check_env.py:583-594`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/check_env.py#L583-L594) is an `if/elif` chain over `is_cuda_v2()/is_hip()/is_npu()/is_musa()/is_mps()` with no `else`, so `env` is never bound and it exits with `NameError: name 'env' is not defined`. Reporting that separately. Environment collected by hand:

```
sglang commit: 0df69849ba
Python:        3.12.13
OS:            Linux-6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2-x86_64-with-glibc2.43
PyTorch:       2.13.0+cpu
transformers:  5.12.1
CUDA available: False
```

The affected code is pure Python request accounting in the scheduler and is exercised by the CPU test suite, so no accelerator is needed to reproduce it.

title: [Feature] Expose the effective `max_running_requests` (after the mamba/linear-attention state-cache cap) in `/get_server_info`
body:
### Checklist
- [x] This is a feature request, not a general question.
- [x] English.

### Motivation
On hybrid (mamba / Gated DeltaNet) models, `KVCacheConfigurator.resolve_max_num_reqs` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`, v0.5.19) can cap concurrency well below the CLI value and only says so in the log:

```
max_running_requests is capped to 9 by the mamba state cache (max_mamba_cache_size=47, 5 state slots per request). To raise it: increase --mamba-full-memory-ratio or --max-mamba-cache-size, or halve the state size with --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16.
```

`GET /get_server_info` keeps returning the CLI value (`"max_running_requests": 32` in our runs), and the ready-summary line (`max_total_num_tokens=... max_running_requests=9 ...`) is again log-only.

Concrete impact: we drove a concurrency benchmark through the OpenAI-compatible API on `Jackrong/Qwopus3.6-27B-v2-FP8` (Qwen3.5-27B hybrid, RTX 6000 Ada 48 GB, `--max-running-requests 32`, default radix cache) across three rentals, believing the server ran 16–32 concurrent requests. It ran 9 and queued the rest. Every "N=16/24/32" number measured the queue, not the engine, and the inflated per-request latency looked like retraction until we read the container log. With `--disable-radix-cache` the per-request slot count drops from 5 to 1 (`_calculate_mamba_ratio`) and the cap disappears — again only visible in the log.

Proposal:
- Add `effective_max_running_requests` to `/get_server_info` (keep the CLI value as-is for compatibility), populated from the value `resolve_max_num_reqs` returns.
- Optionally expose the inputs (`max_mamba_cache_size`, mamba slots per request) so clients can explain the cap, and a gauge in `/metrics` (e.g. `sglang:max_running_requests_effective`).

### Related resources
- `kv_cache_configurator.py::resolve_max_num_reqs` (warning text above) and `_calculate_mamba_ratio` (ratio 3 + 2 with radix cache + overlap schedule; 1 with `--disable-radix-cache`).
- Ready-summary log line: `max_total_num_tokens=... chunked_prefill_size=... max_prefill_tokens=... max_running_requests=<effective> ...`.

title: [Bug] FlashInfer GDN prefill/decode state dtype requirements conflict on SM120
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] This report includes environment info and a minimal reproduction.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.
- [x] This report is in English.

### Describe the bug

On SM120, SGLang accepts `--linear-attn-prefill-backend flashinfer --linear-attn-decode-backend flashinfer --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`, but Qwen3.8-Flash-Next then crashes during warmup because FlashInfer's SM120 GDN prefill path requires FP32 `state_checkpoints`:

```text
sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py:689
sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/gdn_flashinfer.py:332
flashinfer/gdn_prefill.py:289, in chunk_gated_delta_rule
ValueError: state_checkpoints must have dtype float32, got torch.bfloat16
```

Trying to satisfy prefill with `--mamba-ssm-dtype float32` is rejected earlier by SGLang:

```text
ValueError: --linear-attn-decode-backend flashinfer on SM100+ requires
--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16, got 'float32'
```

Therefore FlashInfer prefill + FlashInfer decode has mutually incompatible state-dtype requirements on SM120. The working high-performance configuration is `prefill=triton`, `decode=flashinfer`, `mamba-ssm-dtype=bfloat16`.

At minimum, the invalid all-FlashInfer combination should be rejected during argument resolution on SM120 with an actionable message. Ideally, SGLang should allocate/cast the prefill checkpoint buffer to FP32 independently from the BF16 recurrent-state cache used by FlashInfer decode.

### Reproduction

Image:

```text
lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:12d3392bdc8be8d35e9a95f191df6aef99c5114bdbefd41bfdc7e760e6d25ec1
```

Relevant launch arguments:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 \
  --tp 1 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --ple-offload-embedding \
  --linear-attn-prefill-backend flashinfer \
  --linear-attn-decode-backend flashinfer \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16
```

Changing only `--mamba-ssm-dtype float32` reproduces the argument-validation error above. Changing prefill to Triton while retaining FlashInfer decode and BF16 state passes warmup and inference.

title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next thinking + qwen3_coder tool parser loops on token ID 0
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find this Qwen3.8-Flash-Next failure mode.
- [x] The issue is reproducible on the current day-0 SGLang image used by the official model recipe.
- [x] A minimal request and control request are included below.

## Description

`Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` (also reproducible with the NVFP4 checkpoint `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`) enters a deterministic token-ID-0 repetition loop when all three of these are active:

1. thinking mode (`reasoning_effort` is `low`, `medium`, or `xhigh`),
2. at least one OpenAI-compatible tool is supplied, and
3. SGLang is launched with `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`.

The response starts with valid reasoning and then emits token ID `0` repeatedly. With this tokenizer, token ID 0 decodes as `!`, so the response looks like `The user wants ... tool!!!!!!!!...` until `max_tokens` is reached. No structured tool call is returned.

The same request succeeds immediately when thinking is disabled with `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`. Without `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`, thinking works and the model emits a correct native `<tool_call><function=...>` block, but it is returned as plain content rather than `message.tool_calls`.

## Server command

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.8-flash-next \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --reasoning-parser auto \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --sampling-defaults model \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 30010
```

The server logs correctly auto-detect `reasoning_parser=qwen3` and `tool_call_parser=qwen3_coder` from the chat template.

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:30010/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen3.8-flash-next",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Call shell_probe with command echo parser-ok"}],
    "tools": [{
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "shell_probe",
        "description": "A shell probe tool",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["command"]
        }
      }
    }],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "reasoning_effort": "low",
    "max_tokens": 32,
    "return_token_ids": true,
    "stream": false
  }'
```

Observed output excerpt:

```json
{
  "finish_reason": "length",
  "message": {
    "content": "",
    "reasoning_content": "The user wants me to call the shell_probe tool!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!",
    "tool_calls": null
  },
  "token_ids": [760, 1156, 6587, 728, 310, 1562, 279, 12168, 47460, 5224, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
}
```

## Control: non-thinking succeeds

Using the same request with:

```json
"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}
```

returns:

```json
{
  "finish_reason": "tool_calls",
  "message": {
    "content": "I'll run that command for you.\n\n",
    "reasoning_content": null,
    "tool_calls": [{
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "shell_probe",
        "arguments": "{\"command\": \"echo parser-ok\"}"
      }
    }]
  }
}
```

## Impact

Thinking-mode agent clients such as OpenCode cannot use this model's tools through SGLang. Disabling the parser exposes raw XML; enabling it makes thinking requests loop on token 0. Disabling thinking is a functional regression for this model's intended agentic use.

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, SM120, 96 GB
- Runtime image: `lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:12d3392bdc8be8d35e9a95f191df6aef99c5114bdbefd41bfdc7e760e6d25ec1`
- SGLang commit in image: `d91c3682b`
- CUDA: 13.0.3
- Model: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`
- The official BF16 model uses the same tokenizer/chat template and native `qwen3_coder` XML format.

title: [Bug] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA fallback selects incompatible pip FA4 path on SM120
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] This report includes environment info and a minimal reproduction.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.
- [x] This report is in English.

### Describe the bug

The day-0 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next SGLang image fails during server warmup on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) when Qwen Sparse Attention reaches its packed sparse-decode fallback.

`QwenSparseAttnBackend._resolve_trtllm_sparse_decode()` returns `None` on SM120 because it checks only `is_sm100_supported()`. `_resolve_flash_attn_varlen_func()` then imports `flash_attn.cute.interface` from the pip package. That path compiles a generic/SM100 CUTE kernel and fails for the QSA varlen shape on SM120.

Observed tail of the traceback:

```text
sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py:1741
    output = flash_attn_varlen_func(...)
flash_attn/cute/interface.py
flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd.py:1068
    self.epilogue(...)
flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd.py:393
    mO_cur = seqlen.offset_batch_Q(...)[None, None, head_idx]
...
cutlass._mlir...MLIRError: Operation creation failed:
error: unknown: expects `coord` and shape of view are weakly congruent,
but got '!cute.layout<"(?,?):(?{i64 div=8},1)">', '!cute.coord<"(_,_,?)">'
```

SGLang already contains an SM120-native FA4 dispatcher at `sglang.kernels.ops.attention.flash_attention_v4`. On SM120, changing the QSA fallback to return that wrapper instead of the pip `flash_attn.cute.interface` function fixes startup. With that narrow workaround, the server passed warmup, served a normal completion, sustained ~102.8 decode tokens/s, and completed a 260,000-token prompt.

Suggested direction:

```python
from sglang.srt.utils.common import is_sm120_supported

if is_sm120_supported():
    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.flash_attention_v4 import (
        flash_attn_varlen_func,
    )
```

title: [Bug] NEXTN on B200 silently switches Qwen3.5-122B to triton when --page-size is set; forcing trtllm_mha is 2.6x faster at long context
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

I was running Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 on a rented B200 with and without NEXTN, one request at a time, just to see what speculative decoding does for it. The speculative server came out *slower* than the plain one on long prompts — 119 tok/s vs 229 at ~12k tokens — which seemed backwards, since acceptance was fine (1.7–1.9 tokens per step in the scheduler log).

The `server_args` line explained it. The plain server had picked `attention_backend: trtllm_mha, page_size: 64`; the identical command plus the NEXTN flags had picked `attention_backend: triton, page_size: 1`. Nothing in the log mentions the change. So I put `--attention-backend trtllm_mha` on the speculative command, and it just works — page size stays at 16 and it's flat across context:

| server | ~200 | ~2k | ~12k tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain, auto → `trtllm_mha` | 232.8 | 232.7 | 229.5 |
| plain, `--attention-backend triton` | 224.7 | 210.8 | 159.2 |
| NEXTN, auto → `triton` (page_size 1) | 301.5 | 206.9 | 119.1 |
| NEXTN, `--attention-backend trtllm_mha` forced | **318.4** | **294.3** | **310.7** |

(Batch 1, 128 output tokens, prompts of 186 / 1,862 / 11,150 tokens, tokens counted from `usage.completion_tokens`, radix cache off, a warm-up request then best of two. Same on three separate pods.)

I poked around in v0.5.19 to see where it decides, and I think it's one rule applied to the wrong backend — happy to be corrected:

- `utils/common.py::is_no_spec_infer_or_topk_one` only returns True for topk 1 when `page_size` is 1 or None.
- `arg_groups/model_override_base.py::get_default_attn_backend` only hands out `trtllm_mha` on SM100 when that's True — so with `--page-size 16`, a speculative server never gets it. Its own docstring says the intent is *"Use trtllm_mha for SM100/SM103 ... excluding spec with topk > 1"*, i.e. topk 1 spec should get it.
- `arg_groups/model_overrides/qwen3_5.py::_qwen3_5_hybrid_overrides` then falls back to `triton` and sets `page_size = 1`. Its comment says *"trtllm_mha requires speculative_eagle_topk == 1 and page_size > 1"* — exactly the combination the first rule rejects.
- `arg_groups/overrides.py` accepts 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 for `trtllm_mha`, and my forced run served with 16 without complaint.

If I don't pass `--page-size` at all, the auto path does pick `trtllm_mha`, so the trigger is specifically an explicit page size with topk 1. Per step, `trtllm_mha` does a draft+verify in about 1.35× a plain step at every prompt length; `triton` is 1.40× at 200 tokens and 2.44× at 12k, which is how the auto-selected speculative server ends up slower than no speculation at all.

Other backends, for the record: `fa4` fails at graph capture on this model (`SM100 forward with head_dim=256 does not support seqused_q/seqused_k`; with NEXTN, `q.dtype torch.bfloat16 != k.dtype torch.float8_e4m3fn`), `flashinfer` is refused by the assertion, `fa3` is SM 80–90 only. So `trtllm_mha` is the one backend that runs NEXTN well here, and the one the auto-selector can't reach.

Is that intended — should the topk-1 rule not require `page_size == 1` for a backend that needs `page_size > 1`? Or at least a log line when adding speculation swaps the backend and page size? Workaround for anyone searching: `--attention-backend trtllm_mha`, or leave `--page-size` off.

I've kept the `server_args` lines for all three servers and the fa4 tracebacks if they're useful.

*I used an AI assistant to help with the benchmark harness and to tidy this up; the runs are mine and I can re-run any of them.*

### Reproduction

Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8`, TP=1, one B200.

Plain server (auto-selects `trtllm_mha`, page_size 64):

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --page-size 16 --context-length 32768 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8
```

NEXTN — same flags plus the following (auto-selects `triton`, page_size 1; add `--attention-backend trtllm_mha` and it keeps page_size 16 and runs 2.6× faster at 12k):

```
  --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \
  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-draft-model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 \
  --speculative-num-steps 1 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2
```

Compare the `attention_backend` / `page_size` values in the `server_args` log line of the two servers, then time a single `/v1/completions` request with a ~11k-token prompt and 128 output tokens against each.

### Environment

Image `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19-cu130`, B200 180 GB, RunPod Secure Cloud. The measurements above were on two pods with drivers 595.71.05 / 595.91.07 (host CUDA 13.2); the `check_env` below is from a fresh pod on the same image on a driver-580 host (the first pod I saw this on was also a 580 host).

title: [Bug] Apple Metal (mps) reports no device memory capacity, so mem_fraction_static falls back to 0.95 and prefill OOMs
body:
## Describe the bug

On Apple Silicon, `get_device_memory_capacity()` has no `mps` branch, so it falls through to `gpu_mem = None`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py#L825-L850

That single `None` has two consequences in `handle_gpu_memory_settings` (`python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/memory_hook.py`):

1. The whole `if gpu_mem is not None:` capacity-tier block is skipped, so the per-capacity `chunked_prefill_size` / decode `max_bs` defaults never apply.
2. `mem_fraction_static` takes the `else 0.95` fallback instead of `(gpu_mem - reserved_mem) / gpu_mem`. On every other device `reserved_mem` covers the activation working set (`activation_tokens * 1.5` MB plus a floor); the 0.95 fallback reserves nothing.

The MLX runner then fills that fraction with KV (`_compute_pool_size` in `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/model_runner.py`), leaving ~5% for everything else, and the first real prefill aborts the scheduler:

```
File "python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/mlx/tp_worker.py", line 547, in _async_extend_batch
    mx.async_eval(*async_args)
RuntimeError: [METAL] Command buffer execution failed: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory).

SIGQUIT received. signum=None, frame=None. It usually means one child failed.
```

The sibling function `get_available_gpu_memory()` already carries an `elif device == "mps":` branch (`common.py:534`), which suggests this is an omission rather than a deliberate gap.

## Reproduction

24 GB M-series Mac, macOS 15.7.9, Python 3.12, torch 2.13.0, MLX backend:

```bash
SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit --disable-cuda-graph
```

The server starts and auto-sizes a ~7.2 GB KV pool, then dies on the first non-trivial request.

The resolved configuration can be inspected without launching anything:

```python
from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
from sglang.srt.arg_groups.overrides import resolution_result
from sglang.srt.utils.common import get_device_memory_capacity

sa = ServerArgs(model_path="mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit", disable_cuda_graph=True)
sa.resolve_once()
print(get_device_memory_capacity("mps"))                  # None
print(resolution_result(sa, "device"))                    # 'mps'
print(resolution_result(sa, "mem_fraction_static"))       # 0.95
print(resolution_result(sa, "chunked_prefill_size"))      # 4096
```

`handle_gpu_memory_settings` is reached with the device already resolved, so a `device == "mps"` branch is in time to be used:

```
>>> get_device_memory_capacity(device='mps') -> None
```

## Suggested fix

Metal exposes a recommended working-set size (`torch.mps.recommended_max_memory()`, about two thirds of physical RAM — 16 GB on this 24 GB machine, matching MLX's own `max_recommended_working_set_size`). That cap, not total system memory, is the budget every allocation shares, so reporting it as the device capacity lets the existing reserve formula apply to `mps` like any other device.

With that branch added, the same configuration resolves to `mem_fraction_static=0.773` and `chunked_prefill_size=2048`, and an 8016-token prompt prefills in 2048-token chunks and completes instead of aborting the scheduler.

PR to follow.

## Environment

- SGLang: `main`
- Platform: Apple M-series, 24 GB unified memory, macOS 15.7.9 (arm64)
- Python 3.12.0, torch 2.13.0, MLX backend (`SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`)
- Metal recommended working set: 16.0 GB

title: [Bug][MLX] return_logprob silently returns empty logprobs without --mlx-enable-sampling, so /v1/score answers 500
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On the MLX backend, output logprobs are only computed when `--mlx-enable-sampling` is set (the flag's help text says so, and `MlxTpWorker._logprob_rows` returns `None` unless `_sampling_active(batch)`). Without the flag, a `/generate` request with `return_logprob: true` succeeds and returns empty `output_token_logprobs` / `output_token_ids_logprobs`, with no warning. Nothing tells the caller the option was ignored.

`/v1/score` is built on exactly that (`GenerateReqInput(return_logprob=True, token_ids_logprob=..., max_new_tokens=0)`), so on a default MLX server every `/v1/score` call fails with an opaque 500:

```
RuntimeError: output_logprobs is empty for request <id>.
  File "sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager_score_mixin.py", line 342, in _process_single_item_scoring_results
```

The Apple Metal guide (`docs/hardware-platforms/apple_metal.mdx`) lists the MLX key parameters but not `--mlx-enable-sampling`, so a user following it has no way to know that logprobs and scoring need the flag.

### Reproduction

```bash
SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --disable-cuda-graph --port 30000
```

```python
import requests
r = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:30000/generate", json={
    "text": "Is Paris the capital of France? Answer Yes or No.",
    "return_logprob": True, "token_ids_logprob": [9454, 2753],
    "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0}})
print(r.json()["meta_info"]["output_token_ids_logprobs"])   # []  (also [] for output_token_logprobs)

r = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/score", json={
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "query": "Is Paris the capital of France? Answer",
    "items": [" Yes", " No"], "label_token_ids": [9454, 2753], "apply_softmax": True})
print(r.status_code, r.json())   # 500 {"message": "Internal server error: output_logprobs is empty for request ..."}
```

Relaunching with `--mlx-enable-sampling` makes both work (`/v1/score` returns `[[0.9997, 0.0003], ...]`).

### Suggested fix

Either or both:

1. **Fail fast with a clear message.** `Scheduler.handle_generate_request` already aborts MLX requests that ask for prompt logprobs on the sampling path (`"Prompt input logprobs (logprob_start_len) are not supported on the MLX sampling path..."`). The same spot can abort a request with `return_logprob=True` when the MLX backend is active and `mlx_enable_sampling` is off: `"Output logprobs on the MLX backend require --mlx-enable-sampling."` `/v1/score` would then return that message instead of a 500, and `/generate` callers would stop getting silently empty logprobs.
2. **Document the flag** in the Apple Metal guide's key parameters, next to `SGLANG_MLX_CLEAR_CACHE_STEPS`.

I am happy to open a PR for (1) + (2) if @yeahdongcn agrees with the approach.

### Environment

- SGLang `main` @ 6103a8c743 (editable install, `srt_mps` extra)
- Apple M2, 16 GB, macOS 15.7.5, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.2

title: [Bug] HiCache + hybrid (SSM/Mamba): failed cudaHostRegister on a secondary host pool aborts the whole instance, and the error path throws TypeError thereby hiding the real rc
body:
### Summary

On sglang `0.5.19` (torch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0, H20), starting a **hybrid SSM/Mamba** model
with `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-storage-backend dynamic` fails during
`attach_hybrid_pool_to_unified_cache` and **kills the entire instance**.

Two coupled defects:

1. **`cudaHostRegister` failure is treated as fatal.** `alloc_with_host_register` raises, which
   aborts scheduler init for all TP ranks. But the failure only means "this host pool is not
   zero-copy registered" — and sglang's own non-zero-copy path (`_generic_page_get/_set`) is
   fully functional without registration. A missing acceleration is escalated into a full outage.
2. **The error path destroys its own diagnostic.** Inside the `raise`, `cudart.cudaGetErrorString(rc)`
   is called with a **plain `int`**, which raises `TypeError` on this torch build — so the real
   `rc`/`offset`/`size` are swallowed. Operators only see a bare `TypeError`.

Additionally, the failure **leaves a sticky CUDA error**, which then surfaces later at an unrelated
call site (`_create_sync_groups` → `all_gather_object` → `torch.zeros`), which made this
considerably harder to root-cause.

### Environment

- sglang `0.5.19`
- torch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0
- 8 × H20 (96 GiB) / 8 × H20-3e (141 GiB), driver `535.161.08`
- Model: `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` (`Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`, pool stack **KV + MAMBA**)
- Backend: `--hicache-storage-backend dynamic` with `interface_v1: 1` in the extra config
  (this selects the zero-copy page functions; the crash itself is in host-pool allocation and is
  not specific to any particular dynamic backend)
- Relevant flags: `--mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.37 --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct
  --hicache-io-backend direct --tp 8`

### Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <hybrid SSM/Mamba model, e.g. Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8> \
  --tp-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 1.0 \
  --hicache-storage-backend dynamic \
  --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \
  --hicache-io-backend direct \
  --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.37 \
  --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"backend_name":"...","module_path":"...","class_name":"...","interface_v1":1,...}'
```

Failures are **not deterministic per machine** — we observed the same config **succeed on a 96 GiB
box and fail on a 141 GiB box**, consistent with a pool-geometry / allocation-order dependence.

### Observed failure trace (verbatim)

```
[TP5] attach_hybrid_pool_to_unified_cache failed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 1759, in attach_hybrid_pool_to_unified_cache
    result = strategy.build(
  File ".../hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 1329, in build
    host_pool_group, cache_controller = build_hybrid_mamba_stack(
  File ".../hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 735, in build_hybrid_mamba_stack
    kv_host_pool = build_kv_host_pool(
  File ".../hybrid_pool_assembler.py", line 160, in build_kv_host_pool
    return kv_host_pool_cls(
  File ".../mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py", line 89, in __init__
    super().__init__(
  File ".../mem_cache/pool_host/base.py", line 205, in __init__
    self.kv_buffer = self.init_kv_buffer()
  File ".../mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py", line 191, in init_kv_buffer
    buffer = alloc_func(
  File ".../mem_cache/pool_host/common.py", line 235, in alloc_with_host_register
    _cuda_host_register(buffer, registration_granularity_bytes)
  File ".../mem_cache/pool_host/common.py", line 163, in _cuda_host_register
    f"{cudart.cudaGetErrorString(rc)}) at offset={offset} size={size} "
       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
TypeError: cudaGetErrorString(): incompatible function arguments. The following argument types are supported:
    1. (arg0: torch._C._cudart.cudaError) -> str
Invoked with: 1                      <-- the real rc is only visible here, by accident
```

A second, later-surfacing variant of the same root cause (sticky CUDA error), reached when the
first pool *does* register successfully:

```
[TP6] Scheduler hit an exception: ...
  File ".../mem_cache/hybrid_cache/hybrid_cache_controller.py", line 161, in attach_storage_backend
    super().attach_storage_backend(
  File ".../managers/cache_controller.py", line 590, in attach_storage_backend
    self.prefetch_hits_sync_groups = self._create_sync_groups()
  File ".../managers/cache_controller.py", line 415, in _create_sync_groups
    create_custom_parallel_group(
  File ".../distributed/parallel_state.py", line 2762, in create_custom_parallel_group
    torch.distributed.all_gather_object(gathered_configs, local_config)
  File ".../torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py", line 3506, in all_gather_object
    object_sizes_tensor = torch.zeros(
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

Note `cache_controller.py:590` calls `_create_sync_groups()` **immediately** after the storage
backend is attached — i.e. right where the sticky error from a failed registration lands.

### Minimal evidence that this is the registration call

Instrumenting `_cuda_host_register` on the failing box (141 GiB) shows the KV pool registers fine
and a **secondary** pool is the one that fails:

```
reg#1 total=49676820480 (46.27GiB) granularity=3840        -> OK
reg#2 total=17765498880 (16.55GiB) granularity=11796480    -> FAILED rc=1 (cudaErrorInvalidValue) at offset=0
reg#3 total=623738880  ( 0.58GiB) granularity=414720       -> (never reached)
```

`offset=0`, the size is page aligned, and `chunk_limit=256 GiB` (i.e. a single call) — so this is
**not** an alignment, chunking, or size problem. The same three pools register fine in an
otherwise-idle process, so it is state/order dependent within the real init sequence.

### Minimal standalone reproduction of the underlying CUDA behaviour

The failure mode we traced back to is: calling `cudaHostRegister` on memory that is **already
pinned** returns `cudaErrorInvalidValue(1)` (not `cudaErrorHostMemoryAlreadyRegistered(712)`),
and leaves a sticky error that breaks the next unrelated CUDA call:

```python
import torch
cudart = torch.cuda.cudart()
print("baseline:", float((torch.ones(1024, device="cuda") * 2).sum()))   # works

SZ = 256 * 1024 * 1024
t = torch.empty(SZ, dtype=torch.uint8, pin_memory=True)                   # already pinned
rc = int(cudart.cudaHostRegister(t.data_ptr(), SZ, 0))
print("rc =", rc)                                                          # -> 1 (cudaErrorInvalidValue)

# now any CUDA op fails once:
torch.ones(1024, device="cuda") * 2     # -> AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```
Output on our box:
```
baseline: 2048.0
rc = 1
... torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

### Why we believe the `raise` is not the intended trade-off

`attach_storage_backend` explicitly keeps a **non-zero-copy** default and only opts into
zero-copy afterwards:

```python
self.page_get_func = self._generic_page_get        # default, works without registration
self.page_set_func = self._generic_page_set
if self.storage_backend_type in [...] or (
        self.storage_backend_type == "dynamic"
        and bool(self.storage_config.extra_config.get("interface_v1", 0))):
    self.page_get_func = self._page_get_zero_copy
    self.page_set_func = self._page_set_zero_copy
```

`_generic_page_get` stages through a dummy page and copies in
(`set_from_flat_data_page(...)`) — it does **not** require the host pool to be
`cudaHostRegister`-ed. So "registered" and "correct" are decoupled here: losing the registration
costs the zero-copy fast path, not correctness. Raising therefore converts a **performance
degradation** into an **instance-wide outage**.

The warning text in the raise ("*host buffer is not pinned and device transfers may silently
return stale data*") suggests the intent is to **prevent silent stale reads** — but (a) the
diagnostic it tries to emit is destroyed by the `cudaGetErrorString(int)` `TypeError`, and
(b) there is no degraded path, even though one exists and is safe.

### Suggested fix

**1. Do not `raise` on registration failure — degrade to the non-zero-copy path (main fix).**

```python
rc = int(cudart.cudaHostRegister(ptr, size, 0))
if rc != 0:
    logger.warning(
        "cudaHostRegister failed (rc=%d) at offset=%d size=%d; "
        "this host pool will not be used for zero-copy transfers",
        rc, offset, size,
    )
    _clear_sticky_cuda_error()   # see (2)
    return                        # fall back to the non-registered path
```

**2. Consume the sticky CUDA error before returning**, otherwise the very next collective
(`_create_sync_groups` → `all_gather_object` → `torch.zeros`) still fails. On this torch build a
subsequent CUDA call is enough to consume it, e.g.

```python
try:
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
except Exception:
    pass
```

**3. Fix the error path itself** — pass a `cudaError`, not a raw `int`
(and never let the diagnostic throw):

```python
from torch._C import _cudart
...
f"cudaHostRegister failed (rc={rc}, "
f"{cudart.cudaGetErrorString(_cudart.cudaError(rc))}) at offset={offset} ..."
```

**4. Consider an explicit escape hatch to disable host registration for CUDA.**
`ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS` only maps `npu`/`musa` to `alloc_with_pin_memory`;
on CUDA there is currently no way to opt out other than `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_REGISTER_CHUNK_GB`
(which only changes chunking — we verified setting it to `1` does **not** avoid this failure).

### Evidence that each proposed fix is sound (verified on the failing box)

**Claim 1 — host memory works without `cudaHostRegister` (so degrading is safe).**
Tested each in a fresh process (to avoid sticky-error cross-contamination):

```
mode=pin   (torch pin_memory, no cudaHostRegister at all)
  sum = 4096.0  (expect 4096.0)   is_pinned = True    RESULT: OK

mode=mmap  (plain unregistered host memory, is_pinned = False)
  sum = 4096.0                    RESULT: OK
```
⇒ Neither pinned nor unregistered host memory needs `cudaHostRegister` to move data to the GPU.
Losing the registration only removes the zero-copy fast path.

**Claim 2 — `cudaGetErrorString` needs a `cudaError`, not an `int`.**
```
cudaGetErrorString(1)                    -> TypeError: incompatible function arguments
cudaGetErrorString(_cudart.cudaError(1)) -> "invalid argument"        # correct
```

**Claim 3 — a failed registration leaves a sticky error; `synchronize()` clears it.**
```
baseline GPU op                                  -> 1024.0
cudaHostRegister(already-pinned, 64MiB)         -> rc=1
next GPU op                                     -> AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
torch.cuda.synchronize()                        -> ok
GPU op after synchronize()                      -> 1024.0            # recovered
```

**Claim 4 — `cudaHostUnregister` also returns rc=1 while sticky** (so cleanup of a failed
registration cannot be relied upon to recover the state):
```
cudaHostUnregister(same buffer) -> cudaErrorInvalidValue(1)
```

### Why the existing unit tests did not catch this

`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_host_register.py` (added together with the chunked
registration work) covers the chunking / alignment / rollback logic thoroughly, but two gaps
explain why the real-world failure still slips through:

1. **The failure path is asserted as intended behaviour.** `test_registration_failure_rolls_back_prior_chunks`
   uses `assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "offset=1073741824")` — i.e. the test *encodes* that a
   failed registration must raise. So the question "should it degrade instead of raising?" is a
   **design decision already locked in by a test**, not an oversight I am reporting as a bug.
   (Either way, I'd argue it is the wrong trade-off for the reasons in the Summary — but it is a
   design discussion, so I'm flagging it as such.)
2. **The fake `cudart` accepts an `int` for `cudaGetErrorString`, hiding the real signature:**
   ```python
   class _FakeCudart:
       def cudaGetErrorString(self, rc: int) -> str:      # permissive: accepts int
           return "injected error"
   ```
   The real object is
   `torch._C._cudart.cudart.cudaGetErrorString(arg0: torch._C._cudart.cudaError) -> str`
   and raises `TypeError` when given an `int`. Because the mock is permissive, the `TypeError`
   inside the `raise` can never surface in CI — yet that is precisely the error users see in the
   field, and it is what hides `rc`/`offset`/`size`.

### Affected code ownership (from `git log`, in case it helps routing)

- `_cuda_host_register` / `alloc_with_host_register` + `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_REGISTER_CHUNK_GB`
  came in with **#36798 "[HiCache] Align chunked CUDA host registrations"** (@HZY-Wade), which also
  added the unit test discussed above. That PR's own motivation mentions the same
  `invalid argument` failure mode we are hitting.
- The hybrid pool assembly path (`attach_hybrid_pool_to_unified_cache` /
  `build_hybrid_mamba_stack`) and `pool_host/base.py` are from the unified-memory HiCache work
  (@ch-wan).
- The failing line `attach_storage_backend` → `_create_sync_groups()` in
  `managers/cache_controller.py` is in the HiCache controller (@alphabetc1, @ch-wan).

Pinging @HZY-Wade and @ch-wan as the most likely owners of the affected code — apologies if this
is not your area, and feel free to redirect.

### Impact

- **Hybrid SSM/Mamba models** (which instantiate **multiple** host pools — KV + Mamba/SWA + conv)
  are much more exposed than single-pool attention models, because each additional pool is
  another chance to hit the failing registration. This makes HiCache L3 unusable for that model
  family on affected hardware, with a hard crash rather than a performance warning.
- For production this is a availability issue, and it is **not** diagnosable from the surfaced
  error alone.

### Notes / limitations of this report

- The design-intent reading above is inferred from docstrings, comments, the error text, and the
  existence of the non-zero-copy path — it is not confirmed by maintainers.
- We observed the behaviour on sglang `0.5.19` + torch `2.13.0+cu130`; we have **not** checked
  whether a newer sglang/torch already addresses it.
- We have **not** yet validated end-to-end that "degrade instead of raise" + "clear sticky error"
  yields a fully serving instance on the affected box. What *is* individually verified is:
  the registration failure and its `rc`, the destroyed diagnostic, the sticky error and its
  clearing, and that host memory does not need registration to be usable.
- The exact reason the *second* pool's registration fails is still not fully isolated. It is
  **not** page alignment (`offset=0`), **not** a single-call size limit (64 GiB registers fine
  standalone), **not** a cumulative-size cap (46 GiB then 16 GiB succeeds in a fresh process),
  and **not** chunking (`SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_REGISTER_CHUNK_GB=1` does not avoid it). It appears
  to depend on process state / allocation order during real init.

title: [Bug] Interrupted Mooncake trace download is reused as a complete cache
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

When SGLang downloads a Mooncake JSONL trace and the streamed HTTP response raises an exception after one or more chunks have been written, the partially written destination file is left in place. On the next `MooncakeDataset.load()`, the file-existence check treats that path as an available dataset and skips the download. The benchmark then reads only the records present in the partial file (or fails while parsing a truncated final line) instead of retrying the download.

This report concerns a path written by a failed download. It does not ask SGLang to remove arbitrary pre-existing user-provided dataset files.

### Reproduction

The following CPU-only reproduction uses a temporary destination that does not exist before the first load. The mocked response yields one complete JSONL record and then raises a connection error while the body is being streamed:

```python
import os
import tempfile
from unittest.mock import patch

import requests
from sglang.benchmark.datasets.mooncake import MooncakeDataset


class InterruptedResponse:
    headers = {"content-length": "200"}

    def raise_for_status(self):
        pass

    def iter_content(self, chunk_size):
        yield b'{"timestamp": 1, "hash_ids": []}\n'
        raise requests.exceptions.ConnectionError("simulated interrupted transfer")


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
    path = os.path.join(temp_dir, "trace.jsonl")
    dataset = MooncakeDataset(path, "conversation", 10)

    with patch(
        "sglang.benchmark.utils.requests.get",
        return_value=InterruptedResponse(),
    ):
        try:
            dataset.load()
        except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("the first load should raise ConnectionError")

    print("final path exists:", os.path.exists(path))
    print("rows returned by the next load:", len(dataset.load()))
```

Observed on the commit below:

```text
first load: raises ConnectionError
final path exists: True
rows returned by the next load: 1
```

The second load does not issue another HTTP request because the destination path exists.

### Expected behavior

After a streamed download fails, SGLang should not leave a final path that a later load treats as a complete downloaded dataset. A subsequent load should retry the failed download or report that the downloaded dataset is unavailable; it should not silently benchmark from the partial trace.

### Environment

- SGLang source: `main` at `41812afe432a54308be1c361a4d587952356f958`
- OS: Ubuntu on WSL2, Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64
- Python: 3.12.14
- PyTorch: 2.13.0+cpu; `torch.cuda.is_available() == False`
- No model, server, or GPU is needed for this reproduction.
- `PYTHONPATH=python python -m sglang.check_env` currently fails on this CPU-only environment with `NameError: name 'env' is not defined`; this is unrelated to the reproduction above.

title: [Bug] `--json-model-override-args '{"rope_scaling": ...}'` drops `rope_theta` for models without a per-model fallback: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct GSM8K 161 → 106 (first 200)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Under Transformers v5, assigning `rope_scaling` on a built config replaces `rope_parameters` wholesale, so an
override given with `--json-model-override-args` leaves `rope_parameters` without `rope_theta`. `get_rope_config`
then falls back to 10000. #22739 added a fallback of 1e6 for Qwen3 dense models, which hides the problem there;
Llama (base 500000) and Qwen3-MoE (1e6) are not covered and run with base 10000, with no warning.

### Reproduction

Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, restating the checkpoint's **own** `rope_scaling` (so the override should change nothing):

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct \
  --json-model-override-args '{"rope_scaling": {"rope_type": "llama3", "factor": 32.0, "low_freq_factor": 1.0, "high_freq_factor": 4.0, "original_max_position_embeddings": 8192}}'
```

| run | RoPE base the model runs with | GSM8K (first 200, greedy) |
|---|---|---|
| untouched | 500000 | 161 |
| own `rope_scaling` restated at launch | **10000** (fallback) | **106** |

Outputs stay fluent. The same restatement through `config.json` keeps the base.

**Suggested fix**

When the override dict carries no `rope_theta`, keep the value from the config as loaded from the files before
replacing `rope_parameters` (the `config.json` path already does this), and warn when `rope_parameters` ends up
without a base instead of silently using 10000. A per-model fallback (as in #22739) does not cover checkpoints of
the same architecture with another base (Qwen3-2507: 5e6; Qwen2.5-1M: 1e7).

### Environment

SGLang 0.5.20 (transformers 5.12.1 in that environment at the time of the run), torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12, one RTX
4070 Ti, WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04. Script (`sglang_llama.py`), launch line and raw results:
